use crate::vm::network::NetworkConfig;

/// Local guest account used for PowerShell Direct. The base image must have
/// this account with this password; override with
/// [VmOrchestrator::with_guest_credentials] when it differs.
const DEFAULT_GUEST_USER: &str = "Administrator";
const DEFAULT_GUEST_PASSWORD: &str = "Protocol!2024";

/// Virtual switch used for the loopback pair. Created by network.
const LOOPBACK_SWITCH: &str = "Protocol-Loopback";

/// Startup memory for a freshly provisioned guest.
const PROVISION_MEMORY_BYTES: u64 = 6 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// PowerShell single-quoted literal escaping. Doubles embedded quotes.
fn ps_escape(s: &str) -> String {
s.replace(''', "''")
}

fn run_ps(script: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
let output = Command::new("powershell.exe")
.args([
"-NoProfile",
"-NonInteractive",
"-ExecutionPolicy",
"Bypass",
"-Command",
script,
])
.output()
.map_err(|e| format!("failed to spawn powershell.exe: {}", e))?;

if !output.status.success() {
    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
    return Err(if stderr.is_empty() { stdout } else { stderr });
}

Ok(String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string())
}

/// Locate the base VHDX. Checked in order: explicit override, the working
/// directory (dev runs from src-tauri), then beside the executable
/// (bundled resources land in resources/).
pub fn resolve_base_vhdx() -> Option<PathBuf> {
let candidates = [
std::env::var("PROTOCOL_BASE_VHDX").ok().map(PathBuf::from),
Some(PathBuf::from("resources").join("base.vhdx")),
std::env::current_exe()
.ok()
.and_then(|p| p.parent().map(|d| d.join("resources").join("base.vhdx"))),
];

candidates
    .into_iter()
    .flatten()
    .find(|p| p.exists())
    .map(|p| p.canonicalize().unwrap_or(p))
}

fn vm_state(name: &str) -> Option<String> {
let script = format!(
"(Get-VM -Name '{}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).State.ToString()",
ps_escape(name)
);
let out = run_ps(&script).ok()?;
if out.is_empty() {
None
} else {
Some(out)
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// VM STATUS QUERY
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct VmStatus {
pub running: bool,
pub vm_name: String,
pub state: String,
pub uptime_seconds: u64,
pub cpu_usage: f32,
pub memory_assigned_mb: u64,
pub memory_usage_mb: u64,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct RawVmStatus {
#[serde(rename = "State")]
state: String,
#[serde(rename = "UptimeSeconds", default)]
uptime_seconds: i64,
#[serde(rename = "ProcessorUsage", default)]
cpu_usage: Option<f64>,
#[serde(rename = "MemoryAssigned", default)]
memory_assigned: u64,
#[serde(rename = "MemoryDemand", default)]
memory_demand: u64,
}

fn get_vm_status_blocking(vm_name: String) -> Result<VmStatus, String> {
// Emit flat primitives rather than the raw TimeSpan object, so the host
// side has one unambiguous shape to parse.
let ps_cmd = format!(
r#"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$vm = Get-VM -Name '{vm}' -ErrorAction Stop
[pscustomobject]@{{
State = $vm.State.ToString()
UptimeSeconds = [int64]((Get-Date) - $vm.Uptime).TotalSeconds
ProcessorUsage = [double]$vm.ProcessorUsage
MemoryAssigned = [uint64]$vm.MemoryAssigned
MemoryDemand = [uint64]$vm.MemoryDemand
}} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
"#,
vm = ps_escape(&vm_name)
);

let stdout = match run_ps(&ps_cmd) {
    Ok(s) => s,
    Err(_) => return Ok(not_found(vm_name)),
};

if stdout.is_empty() {
    return Ok(not_found(vm_name));
}

let raw: RawVmStatus = match serde_json::from_str(&stdout) {
    Ok(r) => r,
    Err(_) => return Ok(not_found(vm_name)),
};

let running = raw.state.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Running");

Ok(VmStatus {
    running,
    vm_name,
    state: raw.state,
    uptime_seconds: raw.uptime_seconds.max(0) as u64,
    cpu_usage: raw.cpu_usage.unwrap_or(0.0) as f32,
    memory_assigned_mb: raw.memory_assigned / (1024 * 1024),
    memory_usage_mb: raw.memory_demand / (1024 * 1024),
})
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn get_vm_status(vm_name: String) -> Result<VmStatus, String> {
tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || get_vm_status_blocking(vm_name))
.await
.map_err(|e| format!("status task panicked: {}", e))?
}

fn not_found(vm_name: String) -> VmStatus {
VmStatus {
running: false,
vm_name,
state: "NotFound".to_string(),
uptime_seconds: 0,
cpu_usage: 0.0,
memory_assigned_mb: 0,
memory_usage_mb: 0,
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// VM SPAWN
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct VmSpawnResult {
pub success: bool,
pub vm_name: String,
pub pid: Option<u32>,
pub message: String,
}

/// Provision (if absent) and start the guest, then attach the console.
///
/// A VM that already exists is reused; only the disk work is skipped. Boot is
/// polled rather than slept on, so a fast start returns fast.
fn spawn_blocking_impl(
vm_name: String,
stealth_profile: Option<String>,
) -> Result<VmSpawnResult, String> {
let profile = stealth_profile.unwrap_or_else(|| "default".to_string());
let name = ps_escape(&vm_name);

// ── 1. Provision ─────────────────────────────────────────────
let existing = vm_state(&vm_name);

if existing.is_none() {
    let base = resolve_base_vhdx().ok_or_else(|| {
        "base VHDX not found. Set PROTOCOL_BASE_VHDX or run scripts/create-base-vhdx.ps1."
            .to_string()
    })?;
    let base_literal = ps_escape(&base.to_string_lossy());

    let provision = format!(
        r#"$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$name = '{name}'
$base = '{base}'
$dir = Join-Path $env:ProgramData 'Protocol\VMs'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
$vhd = Join-Path $dir ($name + '.vhdx')
New-VHD -Path $vhd -ParentPath $base -Differencing | Out-Null
New-VM -Name $name -VHDPath $vhd -MemoryStartupBytes {mem} -Generation 2 | Out-Null
Set-VM -Name $name -ProcessorCount 4 -CheckpointType Disabled | Out-Null
Add-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName $name -SwitchName '{switch}' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
"#,
name = name,
base = base_literal,
mem = PROVISION_MEMORY_BYTES,
switch = LOOPBACK_SWITCH
);

run_ps(&provision).map_err(|e| format!("provisioning failed: {}", e))?;
}

// ── 2. Harden (best-effort) ──────────────────────────────────
// `Set-VMHost` is host-wide and needs elevation; a guest that boots
// unhardened still beats no guest.
let harden = format!(
    r#"$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Set-VMProcessor -VMName '{name}' -HideHypervisorPresent $true
Set-VMMemory -VMName '{name}' -DynamicMemoryEnabled $false
"#,
name = name
);
if let Err(e) = run_ps(&harden) {
eprintln!("[vm] hardening failed for '{}': {}", vm_name, e);
}

let _ = run_ps("Set-VMHost -EnableEnhancedSessionMode $false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue");

// ── 3. Start ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
let state = vm_state(&vm_name).unwrap_or_else(|| "Off".to_string());
if !state.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Running") {
    run_ps(&format!("Start-VM -Name '{}'", name))
        .map_err(|e| format!("Start-VM failed: {}", e))?;
}

// ── 4. Poll for Running ──────────────────────────────────────
let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
let mut final_state = state;
while Instant::now() < deadline {
    final_state = vm_state(&vm_name).unwrap_or_else(|| "Unknown".to_string());
    if final_state.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Running") {
        break;
    }
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500));
}

let success = final_state.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Running")
    || final_state.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Starting");

if !success {
    return Ok(VmSpawnResult {
        success: false,
        vm_name: vm_name.clone(),
        pid: None,
        message: format!("VM state: {} (profile: {})", final_state, profile),
    });
}

// ── 5. Attach the console ────────────────────────────────────
let child = Command::new("vmconnect.exe")
    .arg("localhost")
    .arg(&vm_name)
    .spawn()
    .map_err(|e| {
        format!(
            "VM is running but vmconnect failed: {}. Install Hyper-V management tools.",
            e
        )
    })?;

Ok(VmSpawnResult {
    success: true,
    vm_name,
    pid: Some(child.id()),
    message: format!("VM state: {} (profile: {})", final_state, profile),
})
}

/// Blocking form, for callers already on a blocking thread.
pub fn spawn_stealth_vm_blocking(
vm_name: String,
stealth_profile: Option<String>,
) -> Result<VmSpawnResult, String> {
spawn_blocking_impl(vm_name, stealth_profile)
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn spawn_stealth_vm_cmd(
vm_name: String,
stealth_profile: Option<String>,
) -> Result<VmSpawnResult, String> {
tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || spawn_blocking_impl(vm_name, stealth_profile))
.await
.map_err(|e| format!("spawn task panicked: {}", e))?
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// VM SHUTDOWN
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn shutdown_blocking(vm_name: String, force: bool) -> Result<String, String> {
let script = if force {
format!("Stop-VM -Name '{}' -Force -ErrorAction Stop", ps_escape(&vm_name))
} else {
format!("Stop-VM -Name '{}' -ErrorAction Stop", ps_escape(&vm_name))
};

run_ps(&script).map_err(|e| format!("shutdown failed: {}", e))?;
Ok(format!("VM '{}' shutdown initiated", vm_name))
}

#[tauri::command]
pub async fn shutdown_vm(vm_name: String, force: Option<bool>) -> Result<String, String> {
let force = force.unwrap_or(false);
tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || shutdown_blocking(vm_name, force))
.await
.map_err(|e| format!("shutdown task panicked: {}", e))?
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ORCHESTRATOR STATE MACHINE
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Represents the lifecycle state of the ephemeral sandbox.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum VmState {
Offline,
Provisioning,
Booting,
Running,
Hooked,
Nuked,
Error(String),
}

/// The central controller for spinning up and tearing down the localized matrix.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub struct VmOrchestrator {
pub profile: TargetProfile,
pub vm_name: String,
pub state: Arc<Mutex<VmState>>,
pub loopback_ip: String,
pub guest_username: String,
pub guest_password: String,
}

#[allow(dead_code)]
pub struct Vm {
pub vm_name: String,
pub loopback_ip: String,
}

impl Vm {
pub async fn create_differencing_disk(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
let base = resolve_base_vhdx()
.ok_or_else(|| "base VHDX not found".to_string())?;
let output_dir = std::env::var("ProgramData")
.map(|p| PathBuf::from(p).join("Protocol").join("VMs"))
.map_err(|_| "ProgramData unset".to_string())?;

clone::create_differencing_disk(&self.vm_name, &base, &output_dir)
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

pub async fn configure_loopback_adapter(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
    network::configure_loopback_adapter(&NetworkConfig::default()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}
}

impl VmOrchestrator {
/// Initializes a new orchestrator for a specific proctoring target.
pub fn new(profile: TargetProfile) -> Self {
// Pseudo-random name to avoid Hyper-V collisions and defeat
// static-string host scans.
let entropy = Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
let vm_name = format!("win_sys_{}", &entropy[..8]);

Self {
        profile,
        vm_name,
        state: Arc::new(Mutex::new(VmState::Offline)),
        loopback_ip: "127.0.0.2".to_string(),
        guest_username: DEFAULT_GUEST_USER.to_string(),
        guest_password: DEFAULT_GUEST_PASSWORD.to_string(),
    }
}

/// Override the guest credentials used for PowerShell Direct.
pub fn with_guest_credentials(
    mut self,
    username: impl Into<String>,
    password: impl Into<String>,
) -> Self {
    self.guest_username = username.into();
    self.guest_password = password.into();
    self
}

/// Main ignition sequence — full deployment pipeline.
pub async fn engage(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
    {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().await;
        *state = VmState::Provisioning;
    }

    let _cfg = config::build_config(&self.profile.display_name);

    network::configure_loopback_adapter(&NetworkConfig::default())
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().await;
        *state = VmState::Booting;
    }

    hyperv::HyperVOrchestrator::new(&self.vm_name)
        .start()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    lifecycle::wait_for_boot(&self.loopback_ip)
        .await
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    {
        let mut state = self.state.lock().await;
        *state = VmState::Running;
    }

    Ok(())
}

/// Injects target-specific kernel and registry patches via PowerShell remoting.
pub async fn apply_stealth_hooks(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut state = self.state.lock().await;

    // Wire to crate::patches::loader once the injection API lands; the
    // profile carries the patch_set_id the loader needs.
    *state = VmState::Hooked;
    Ok(())
}

/// Completely obliterates the VM, differencing disk, and vSwitch.
pub async fn teardown(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
    lifecycle::destroy_vm(&self.vm_name, None).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    network::destroy_network(&network::get_network_config()).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    let mut state = self.state.lock().await;
    *state = VmState::Nuked;
    Ok(())
}

/// Returns current state for the frontend telemetry feed.
pub async fn get_status(&self) -> VmState {
    self.state.lock().await.clone()
}
}

//! src-tauri/src/hyper_v/vm_manager.rs
//!
//! Guest interaction surface.
//!
//! Everything the artifact cleaner needs from a VM goes through
//! [VmManagerOps]: liveness, in-guest execution, and file movement. The trait
//! exists so the cleaner can be driven by MockVmManager in tests without a
//! hypervisor.
//!
//! Methods return boxed futures rather than being plain async fn because the
//! cleaner stores Box<dyn VmManagerOps> — native async-in-trait is not
//! object-safe.

use async_trait::async_trait;

use crate::stealth::StealthError;
use crate::util::ps_literal;
use crate::util::powershell::PowerShellScript;

use super::{build_guest_invocation, run_host_ps, run_host_ps_transfer, GuestCredentials};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Contract
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Host-side operations against a single guest VM.
///
/// Every method takes the VM name explicitly rather than being bound to one
/// VM, so a single manager can serve several guests.
#[cfg_attr(test, mockall::automock)]
#[async_trait]
pub trait VmManagerOps: Send + Sync {
/// Whether the named VM exists and is currently running.
///
/// A missing VM is Ok(false), not an error — callers distinguish
/// "absent" from "the host is broken".
async fn is_vm_running(&self, vm_name: &str) -> Result<bool, StealthError>;

/// Execute a PowerShell script inside the guest and return its output.
///
/// Requires PowerShell Direct, i.e. the guest must be running and the
/// supplied credentials must be local administrators.
async fn execute_in_guest(
    &self,
    vm_name: &str,
    script: PowerShellScript,
) -> Result<String, StealthError>;

/// Copy a file out of the guest onto the host.
async fn copy_file_from_guest(
    &self,
    vm_name: &str,
    guest_path: &str,
    host_path: &str,
) -> Result<(), StealthError>;

/// Copy a file from the host into the guest.
async fn copy_file_to_guest(
    &self,
    vm_name: &str,
    host_path: &str,
    guest_path: &str,
) -> Result<(), StealthError>;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Implementation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Real manager, backed by the Hyper-V PowerShell surface.
///
/// File movement uses Copy-VMFile, which depends on the Guest Service
/// Interface integration component being enabled in the guest. Script execution
/// does not — it uses PowerShell Direct instead.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct VmManager {
credentials: GuestCredentials,
}

impl VmManager {
pub fn new() -> Self {
Self::default()
}

/// Use explicit guest credentials instead of the image defaults.
pub fn with_credentials(mut self, credentials: GuestCredentials) -> Self {
    self.credentials = credentials;
    self
}

/// Fail early with a specific error when the guest cannot take a
/// PowerShell Direct session, rather than letting `Invoke-Command`
/// produce an opaque transport fault.
async fn require_running(&self, vm_name: &str) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
    if self.is_vm_running(vm_name).await? {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(StealthError::InvalidHandle(format!(
            "VM '{}' is not running",
            vm_name
        )))
    }
}
}

#[async_trait]
impl VmManagerOps for VmManager {
async fn is_vm_running(&self, vm_name: &str) -> Result<bool, StealthError> {
let script = format!(
r#"$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$vm = Get-VM -Name {vm} -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
if ($null -eq $vm) {{ 'NotFound' }} else {{ $vm.State.ToString() }}
"#,
vm = ps_literal(vm_name)
);

let state = run_host_ps(&script).await?;
    Ok(state.eq_ignore_ascii_case("Running"))
}

async fn execute_in_guest(
    &self,
    vm_name: &str,
    script: PowerShellScript,
) -> Result<String, StealthError> {
    self.require_running(vm_name).await?;

    let invocation = build_guest_invocation(vm_name, &self.credentials, script.as_string());
    run_host_ps(&invocation).await
}

async fn copy_file_from_guest(
    &self,
    vm_name: &str,
    guest_path: &str,
    host_path: &str,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
    self.require_running(vm_name).await?;

    let script = format!(
        r#"$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Copy-VMFile -VMName {vm} -SourcePath {src} -DestinationPath {dst} `
-FileSource Guest -Force -CreateFullPath -ErrorAction Stop
"#,
vm = ps_literal(vm_name),
src = ps_literal(guest_path),
dst = ps_literal(host_path),
);

run_host_ps_transfer(&script).await.map(|_| ())
}

async fn copy_file_to_guest(
    &self,
    vm_name: &str,
    host_path: &str,
    guest_path: &str,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
    self.require_running(vm_name).await?;

    let script = format!(
        r#"$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Copy-VMFile -VMName {vm} -SourcePath {src} -DestinationPath {dst} `
-FileSource Host -Force -CreateFullPath -ErrorAction Stop
"#,
vm = ps_literal(vm_name),
src = ps_literal(host_path),
dst = ps_literal(guest_path),
);

run_host_ps_transfer(&script).await.map(|_| ())
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
use super::*;

#[test]
fn manager_defaults_to_image_credentials() {
    let manager = VmManager::new();
    assert_eq!(manager.credentials.username(), r".\Administrator");
}

#[test]
fn credentials_are_overridable() {
    let manager = VmManager::new().with_credentials(GuestCredentials::new("bob", "pw"));
    assert_eq!(manager.credentials.username(), r".\bob");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn mock_satisfies_the_object_safe_trait() {
    let mut mock = MockVmManager::new();
    mock.expect_is_vm_running()
        .returning(|_| Box::pin(async { Ok(true) }));

    let boxed: Box<dyn VmManagerOps> = Box::new(mock);
    assert!(boxed.is_vm_running("Anything").await.unwrap());
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public entrypoint / bootstrapping
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Convenience bootstrap: apply a baseline patch set using the given AppHandle.
/// The actual target is resolved via build_config + the loader.
pub async fn bootstrap_default(app_handle: &AppHandle) {
let target_id = "MSB"; // Default target ID — override via IPC command for real runs.
let vm_config = build_config(target_id);

if let Err(e) = loader::apply_patches(vec![], &vm_config).await {
    eprintln!(
        "[stealth::bootstrap_default] Failed to apply patches: {}",
        e
    );
} else {
    println!(
        "[stealth::bootstrap_default] Patches applied successfully for '{}'.",
        target_id
    );
}

// Reserved for future IPC event emission.
let _ = app_handle;
}

/// Block-on helper for sync contexts that need to call async code.
/// MUST be invoked from within a Tokio runtime.
pub(crate) fn block_on<F: std::future::Future>(fut: F) -> F::Output {
tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(fut)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// StealthCheck / StealthPosture — IPC-exposed health report
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct StealthCheck {
pub check_name: String,
pub passed: bool,
pub status: String,
pub remediation: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize)]
pub struct StealthPosture {
pub overall_score: u8,
pub total_checks: usize,
pub passed_checks: usize,
pub failed_checks: usize,
pub checks: Vec<StealthCheck>,
pub posture_level: String,
}

/// Substring match against a process name, using an already-refreshed table.
///
/// Takes the System by reference: the posture sweep runs eleven of these, and
/// rebuilding the table per call would re-enumerate every process each time.
fn process_running(sys: &System, signature: &str) -> bool {
let needle = signature.to_lowercase();
sys.processes()
.values()
.any(|p| p.name().to_lowercase().contains(&needle))
}

fn powershell_scalar(script: &str) -> String {
Command::new("powershell")
.args(["-NoProfile", "-Command", script])
.output()
.map(|o| String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout).trim().to_string())
.unwrap_or_default()
}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn verify_stealth_posture() -> Result<StealthPosture, String> {
let mut checks: Vec<StealthCheck> = Vec::new();

// One process snapshot for every process-based check below.
let mut sys = System::new_all();
sys.refresh_processes();

// Check 1: Hyper-V management service
let hyperv_running = process_running(&sys, "vmms");
checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "hyperv_management".to_string(),
    passed: true,
    status: if hyperv_running {
        "Hyper-V VM Management running (normal)".to_string()
    } else {
        "Hyper-V VM Management not running — VMs won't start".to_string()
    },
    remediation: if !hyperv_running {
        Some("Start-Service vmms".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    },
});

// Check 2: RDP / VMConnect window available for optical capture
let rdp_procs = ["mstsc", "vmconnect", "rdpclient"];
let rdp_found = rdp_procs.iter().any(|p| process_running(&sys, p));
checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "rdp_window_present".to_string(),
    passed: rdp_found,
    status: if rdp_found {
        "RDP/VM window process detected — capture available".to_string()
    } else {
        "No RDP or VMConnect window open — nothing to capture".to_string()
    },
    remediation: if !rdp_found {
        Some("Start the RDP session or launch VMConnect before activating overlay".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    },
});

// Check 3: Proctoring software detection (informational)
let proctor_sigs = [
    "proctorio",
    "honorlock",
    "proctoru",
    "respondus",
    "lockdownbrowser",
    "examity",
    "testinvite",
];
let running_proctors: Vec<String> = proctor_sigs
    .iter()
    .filter(|sig| process_running(&sys, sig))
    .map(|s| s.to_string())
    .collect();

checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "proctoring_software".to_string(),
    passed: true,
    status: if running_proctors.is_empty() {
        "No proctoring software detected on Host".to_string()
    } else {
        format!(
            "Active proctoring: {} (Guest-side only — optical gap holds)",
            running_proctors.join(", ")
        )
    },
    remediation: None,
});

// Check 4: Overlay WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE
let overlay_script = r#"
    Add-Type -TypeDefinition @'
    using System;
    using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
    public class Win32 {
        [DllImport("user32.dll")]
        public static extern int GetWindowLong(IntPtr hWnd, int nIndex);
        [DllImport("user32.dll")]
        public static extern int GetWindowDisplayAffinity(IntPtr hWnd, out uint affinity);
    }
'@
$proc = Get-Process | Where-Object { $.MainWindowTitle -ne '' -and $.ProcessName -match 'protocol|tauri' } | Select-Object -First 1
if ($proc) {
$hwnd = $proc.MainWindowHandle
$affinity = 0
[Win32]::GetWindowDisplayAffinity($hwnd, [ref]$affinity) | Out-Null
Write-Output $affinity
} else {
Write-Output 'no-window'
}
"#;

let affinity_result = powershell_scalar(overlay_script);
let overlay_protected = affinity_result == "17"; // WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE = 0x11
checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "overlay_capture_protection".to_string(),
    passed: overlay_protected,
    status: match affinity_result.as_str() {
        "17" => "WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE active — overlay invisible to screen share".to_string(),
        "no-window" => "Overlay window not found — is the app running?".to_string(),
        "0" => "Overlay visible to capture APIs — NOT protected".to_string(),
        other => format!("Display affinity returned: {}", other),
    },
    remediation: if !overlay_protected {
        Some("Ensure Windows 10 2004+ and overlay is calling SetWindowDisplayAffinity(WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE)".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    },
});

// Check 5: Loopback adapter
let adapter_result = powershell_scalar(
    "(Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object { $_.Name -match 'Loopback|Protocol' } | Measure-Object).Count",
);
let tunnel_ready = adapter_result.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0) > 0;
checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "loopback_tunnel".to_string(),
    passed: true,
    status: if tunnel_ready {
        "Loopback adapter present — tunnel mode available".to_string()
    } else {
        "No loopback adapter — tunnel mode unavailable (local capture still works)".to_string()
    },
    remediation: if !tunnel_ready {
        Some("Run start_loopback_tunnel to provision the adapter".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    },
});

// Check 6: RDP listener on 3389
let port_check = std::net::TcpStream::connect_timeout(
    &"127.0.0.1:3389"
        .parse::<std::net::SocketAddr>()
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
    std::time::Duration::from_millis(300),
)
.is_ok();

checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "rdp_listener".to_string(),
    passed: port_check,
    status: if port_check {
        "RDP listener active on 3389".to_string()
    } else {
        "RDP not listening on 3389 — Guest connection may fail".to_string()
    },
    remediation: if !port_check {
        Some("Enable RDP in Guest OS or use vmconnect instead".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    },
});

// Check 7: Defender real-time
let defender_result = powershell_scalar(
    "(Get-MpPreference | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DisableRealtimeMonitoring)",
);
let defender_off = defender_result.contains("True");
checks.push(StealthCheck {
    check_name: "defender_realtime".to_string(),
    passed: true,
    status: if defender_off {
        "Defender real-time monitoring disabled".to_string()
    } else {
        "Defender real-time monitoring ACTIVE — may scan overlay binary".to_string()
    },
    remediation: if !defender_off {
        Some("Add exclusion folder for the protocol binary if scans cause lag".to_string())
    } else {
        None
    },
});

let passed = checks.iter().filter(|c| c.passed).count();
let total = checks.len();
let failed = total - passed;

let score = ((passed as f32 / total as f32) * 100.0) as u8;
let posture_level = match score {
    90..=100 => "GREEN".to_string(),
    70..=89 => "YELLOW".to_string(),
    0..=69 => "RED".to_string(),
    _ => "UNKNOWN".to_string(),
};

Ok(StealthPosture {
    overall_score: score,
    total_checks: total,
    passed_checks: passed,
    failed_checks: failed,
    checks,
    posture_level,
})
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// StealthError — canonical error type for the stealth subsystem
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum StealthError {
#[error("VM handle invalid or VM not running: {0}")]
InvalidHandle(String),

#[error("PowerShell execution failed (exit {exit_code}): {stderr}")]
PowerShellFailure { exit_code: i32, stderr: String },

#[error("Target profile missing required stealth configuration: {0}")]
MissingConfig(String),

#[error("CPUID mask application failed: {0}")]
CpuidFailure(String),

#[error("Hardware spoofing failed for device class '{device_class}': {reason}")]
HardwareFailure { device_class: String, reason: String },

#[error("Artifact cleanup failed for registry key '{key}': {reason}")]
ArtifactFailure { key: String, reason: String },

#[error("Timing normalization failed: {0}")]
TimingFailure(String),

#[error("Partial application: {applied}/{total} stealth layers succeeded")]
PartialApplication { applied: usize, total: usize },

#[error("VM went offline during stealth application")]
VmLost,

#[error("Script execution failed: {0}")]
ScriptFailure(String),

#[error("Verification failed: {0}")]
VerificationFailed(String),

#[error("Host invocation error: {0}")]
HostInvocation(String),

/// Guest artifact sweep failure. Carried as the concrete error rather
/// than a string so callers can inspect the variant; the conversion
/// itself lives in artifact.rs.
#[error("Guest artifact error: {0}")]
GuestArtifact(GuestArtifactError),

/// Guest Services / PowerShell Direct transport fault.
#[error("Guest services error: {0}")]
GuestServices(String),

#[error("Session not found: {id}")]
SessionNotFound { id: Uuid },

#[error("Invalid transition from {from} to {to}")]
InvalidTransition { from: String, to: String },

#[error("IO error: {0}")]
Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

#[error("Internal error: {0}")]
Internal(String),
}

pub type StealthResult<T> = Result<T, StealthError>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// StealthLayer — layer identifiers + ordering
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum StealthLayer {
CpuIdMask,
HardwareSpoof,
ArtifactCleanup,
TimingNormalize,
}

impl StealthLayer {
pub const ALL: [StealthLayer; 4] = [
StealthLayer::CpuIdMask,
StealthLayer::HardwareSpoof,
StealthLayer::ArtifactCleanup,
StealthLayer::TimingNormalize,
];

pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {
    match self {
        StealthLayer::CpuIdMask => "cpuid_mask",
        StealthLayer::HardwareSpoof => "hardware_spoof",
        StealthLayer::ArtifactCleanup => "artifact_cleanup",
        StealthLayer::TimingNormalize => "timing_normalize",
    }
}

pub fn execution_order(&self) -> u8 {
    match self {
        StealthLayer::CpuIdMask => 0,
        StealthLayer::HardwareSpoof => 1,
        StealthLayer::ArtifactCleanup => 2,
        StealthLayer::TimingNormalize => 3,
    }
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// StealthRequirements — derived from TargetProfile
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StealthRequirements {
pub layers: Option<Vec<StealthLayer>>,
pub skip_timing: bool,
pub force_hardware_spoof: bool,
}

impl Default for StealthRequirements {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
layers: None,
skip_timing: false,
force_hardware_spoof: false,
}
}
}

impl StealthRequirements {
pub fn from_profile(profile: &TargetProfile) -> Self {
let dv = &profile.detection_vectors;
let dv_kinds = dv.kinds();

let needs_timing_spoof = profile
        .vm_config_override
        .as_ref()
        .map(|c| c.strict_timing_spoof)
        .unwrap_or(false);

    let skip_timing = !needs_timing_spoof;

    let mut layers: Vec<StealthLayer> = StealthLayer::ALL.to_vec();

    if skip_timing {
        layers.retain(|l| *l != StealthLayer::TimingNormalize);
    }

    let force_hardware_spoof = profile.patch_set_id == "generic"
        || profile.target_id == TargetId::Generic
        || dv_kinds.is_empty();

    Self {
        layers: Some(layers),
        skip_timing,
        force_hardware_spoof,
    }
}

fn ordered_layers(&self) -> Vec<StealthLayer> {
    let mut layers: Vec<StealthLayer> = self
        .layers
        .clone()
        .unwrap_or_else(|| StealthLayer::ALL.to_vec());
    layers.sort_by_key(|l| l.execution_order());
    layers.dedup();
    layers
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Session support types — state machine, counters, detections
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SessionState {
Initializing,
Active,
Degraded,
Suspended,
Compromised,
Terminated,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Countermeasure {
CpuidSpoof,
HardwareSpoof,
ArtifactCleanup,
TimingNormalize,
Custom,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Severity {
Low,
Medium,
High,
Critical,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct DetectionEvent {
pub timestamp: u64,
pub vector: DetectionVector,
pub severity: Severity,
pub source: String,
pub details: String,
}

impl DetectionEvent {
pub fn new(
vector: DetectionVector,
severity: Severity,
source: impl Into<String>,
details: impl Into<String>,
) -> Self {
Self {
timestamp: SystemTime::now()
.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
.unwrap_or_default()
.as_secs(),
vector,
severity,
source: source.into(),
details: details.into(),
}
}
}

/// Per-session stealth profile — thresholds and defaults used by the session
/// state machine. Default keeps a sane failure threshold so a session is not
/// instantly marked compromised.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StealthProfile {
pub failure_threshold: u32,
pub patch_set_id: String,
}

impl Default for StealthProfile {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
failure_threshold: 3,
patch_set_id: "generic".to_string(),
}
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// StealthReport / StealthSession — per-run state tracking
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct StealthReport {
pub target_id: String,
pub applied_layers: Vec<StealthLayer>,
pub failed_layers: Vec<(StealthLayer, String)>,
pub duration_ms: u128,
}

impl StealthReport {
pub fn fully_applied(&self) -> bool {
self.failed_layers.is_empty()
}
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct StealthSession {
pub report: StealthReport,
pub session_id: Uuid,
pub profile: StealthProfile,
pub target_id: TargetId,
pub created_at: u64,
pub last_activity: u64,
pub active_countermeasures: Vec<Countermeasure>,
pub detection_events: Vec<DetectionEvent>,
pub success_count: u32,
pub failure_count: u32,
pub state: SessionState,
}

pub type SharedSession = Arc<RwLock<StealthSession>>;

impl StealthSession {
pub fn new(profile: StealthProfile, target_id: TargetId) -> Self {
let now = SystemTime::now()
.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
.unwrap_or_default()
.as_secs();

Self {
        report: StealthReport::default(),
        session_id: Uuid::new_v4(),
        profile,
        target_id,
        created_at: now,
        last_activity: now,
        active_countermeasures: Vec::new(),
        detection_events: Vec::new(),
        success_count: 0,
        failure_count: 0,
        state: SessionState::Initializing,
    }
}

pub fn record_success(&mut self, countermeasure: Countermeasure) {
    self.success_count = self.success_count.saturating_add(1);
    self.touch();
    if !self.active_countermeasures.contains(&countermeasure) {
        self.active_countermeasures.push(countermeasure);
    }
}

pub fn record_failure(&mut self, event: DetectionEvent) {
    self.failure_count = self.failure_count.saturating_add(1);
    self.detection_events.push(event);
    self.touch();

    if self.failure_count >= self.profile.failure_threshold {
        self.state = SessionState::Compromised;
    }
}

pub fn touch(&mut self) {
    self.last_activity = SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .as_secs();
}

pub fn transition(&mut self, new_state: SessionState) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
    use SessionState::*;

    let valid = matches!(
        (&self.state, &new_state),
        (Initializing, Active)
            | (Active, Degraded)
            | (Active, Suspended)
            | (Degraded, Active)
            | (Degraded, Compromised)
            | (Suspended, Active)
            | (Suspended, Terminated)
            | (_, Terminated)
            | (_, Compromised)
    );

    if !valid {
        return Err(StealthError::InvalidTransition {
            from: format!("{:?}", self.state),
            to: format!("{:?}", new_state),
        });
    }

    self.state = new_state;
    self.touch();
    Ok(())
}

pub fn is_viable(&self) -> bool {
    matches!(self.state, SessionState::Active | SessionState::Degraded)
}

pub fn success_rate(&self) -> f64 {
    let total = self.success_count + self.failure_count;
    if total == 0 {
        return 1.0;
    }
    self.success_count as f64 / total as f64
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Session Manager
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct StealthManager {
sessions: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<Uuid, StealthSession>>>,
default_profile: StealthProfile,
metrics: Arc<RwLock<StealthMetrics>>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StealthMetrics {
pub total_sessions: u64,
pub active_sessions: u64,
pub compromised_sessions: u64,
pub total_detections: u64,
pub total_successes: u64,
}

impl StealthManager {
pub fn new() -> Self {
Self {
sessions: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),
default_profile: StealthProfile::default(),
metrics: Arc::new(RwLock::new(StealthMetrics::default())),
}
}

pub fn with_profile(default_profile: StealthProfile) -> Self {
    Self {
        sessions: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),
        default_profile,
        metrics: Arc::new(RwLock::new(StealthMetrics::default())),
    }
}

/// Create a session from the manager's default profile.
pub async fn create_session(&self, target_id: TargetId) -> StealthResult<Uuid> {
    self.create_session_with_profile(target_id, self.default_profile.clone())
        .await
}

/// Create a session with an explicit profile. The session starts in
/// `Initializing` and must be activated explicitly.
pub async fn create_session_with_profile(
    &self,
    target_id: TargetId,
    profile: StealthProfile,
) -> StealthResult<Uuid> {
    if profile.failure_threshold == 0 {
        return Err(StealthError::MissingConfig(
            "failure_threshold must be greater than zero".to_string(),
        ));
    }

    let session = StealthSession::new(profile, target_id);
    let id = session.session_id;

    {
        let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
        sessions.insert(id, session);
    }

    {
        let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
        m.total_sessions = m.total_sessions.saturating_add(1);
    }

    Ok(id)
}

pub async fn get_session(&self, id: Uuid) -> StealthResult<StealthSession> {
    let sessions = self.sessions.read().await;
    sessions
        .get(&id)
        .cloned()
        .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })
}

/// Mutate a session in place under the write lock.
pub async fn with_session_mut<F, T>(&self, id: Uuid, f: F) -> StealthResult<T>
where
    F: FnOnce(&mut StealthSession) -> T,
{
    let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
    let session = sessions
        .get_mut(&id)
        .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })?;
    Ok(f(session))
}

pub async fn activate_session(&self, id: Uuid) -> StealthResult<()> {
    let previous = {
        let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
        let session = sessions
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })?;
        let previous = session.state;
        session.transition(SessionState::Active)?;
        previous
    };

    if previous == SessionState::Initializing {
        let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
        m.active_sessions = m.active_sessions.saturating_add(1);
    }

    Ok(())
}

pub async fn terminate_session(&self, id: Uuid) -> StealthResult<()> {
    let (was_active, was_compromised) = {
        let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
        let session = sessions
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })?;
        let was_active = matches!(session.state, SessionState::Active | SessionState::Degraded);
        let was_compromised = session.state == SessionState::Compromised;
        session.transition(SessionState::Terminated)?;
        (was_active, was_compromised)
    };

    let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
    if was_active {
        m.active_sessions = m.active_sessions.saturating_sub(1);
    }
    if was_compromised {
        m.compromised_sessions = m.compromised_sessions.saturating_sub(1);
    }

    Ok(())
}

pub async fn remove_session(&self, id: Uuid) -> StealthResult<()> {
    let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
    sessions
        .remove(&id)
        .map(|_| ())
        .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })
}

pub async fn list_sessions(&self) -> Vec<Uuid> {
    let sessions = self.sessions.read().await;
    sessions.keys().copied().collect()
}

pub async fn session_count(&self) -> usize {
    self.sessions.read().await.len()
}

// -- detection + countermeasure accounting ------------------------------

pub async fn record_detection(
    &self,
    id: Uuid,
    event: DetectionEvent,
) -> StealthResult<SessionState> {
    let (state, newly_compromised) = {
        let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
        let session = sessions
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })?;

        let was_compromised = session.state == SessionState::Compromised;
        session.record_failure(event);
        let now_compromised = session.state == SessionState::Compromised;

        (session.state, !was_compromised && now_compromised)
    };

    {
        let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
        m.total_detections = m.total_detections.saturating_add(1);
        // Only count the transition, so repeat detections don't inflate
        // the compromised gauge.
        if newly_compromised {
            m.compromised_sessions = m.compromised_sessions.saturating_add(1);
        }
    }

    Ok(state)
}

pub async fn record_success(
    &self,
    id: Uuid,
    countermeasure: Countermeasure,
) -> StealthResult<()> {
    {
        let mut sessions = self.sessions.write().await;
        let session = sessions
            .get_mut(&id)
            .ok_or(StealthError::SessionNotFound { id })?;
        session.record_success(countermeasure);
    }

    let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
    m.total_successes = m.total_successes.saturating_add(1);
    Ok(())
}

// -- metrics ------------------------------------------------------------

pub async fn metrics_snapshot(&self) -> StealthMetrics {
    self.metrics.read().await.clone()
}

pub async fn reset_metrics(&self) {
    let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
    *m = StealthMetrics::default();
}

/// Recompute derived gauges (active/compromised) from live sessions rather
/// than trusting the incrementally maintained counters.
pub async fn reconcile_metrics(&self) -> StealthMetrics {
    let sessions = self.sessions.read().await;

    let active = sessions
        .values()
        .filter(|s| matches!(s.state, SessionState::Active | SessionState::Degraded))
        .count() as u64;
    let compromised = sessions
        .values()
        .filter(|s| s.state == SessionState::Compromised)
        .count() as u64;
    let detections: u64 = sessions
        .values()
        .map(|s| s.detection_events.len() as u64)
        .sum();
    let successes: u64 = sessions.values().map(|s| s.success_count as u64).sum();
    let total = sessions.len() as u64;

    drop(sessions);

    let mut m = self.metrics.write().await;
    m.total_sessions = m.total_sessions.max(total);
    m.active_sessions = active;
    m.compromised_sessions = compromised;
    m.total_detections = detections;
    m.total_successes = successes;
    m.clone()
}
}

impl Default for StealthManager {
fn default() -> Self {
Self::new()
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Posture checks against a live session
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

impl StealthManager {
pub async fn posture_for(&self, id: Uuid) -> StealthResult<StealthPosture> {
let session = self.get_session(id).await?;

let mut checks = Vec::new();

    checks.push(StealthCheck {
        check_name: "session_state".to_string(),
        passed: session.is_viable(),
        status: format!("Session state: {:?}", session.state),
        remediation: (!session.is_viable())
            .then(|| "Activate or restore the session before relying on it".to_string()),
    });

    checks.push(StealthCheck {
        check_name: "failure_budget".to_string(),
        passed: session.failure_count < session.profile.failure_threshold,
        status: format!(
            "{}/{} failures before compromise",
            session.failure_count, session.profile.failure_threshold
        ),
        remediation: (session.failure_count >= session.profile.failure_threshold)
            .then(|| "Reapply stealth layers or start a fresh session".to_string()),
    });

    checks.push(StealthCheck {
        check_name: "countermeasure_coverage".to_string(),
        passed: !session.active_countermeasures.is_empty(),
        status: format!(
            "{} countermeasure(s) reported",
            session.active_countermeasures.len()
        ),
        remediation: session.active_countermeasures.is_empty().then(|| {
            "Report at least one successful countermeasure application".to_string()
        }),
    });

    let total = checks.len();
    let passed = checks.iter().filter(|c| c.passed).count();
    let failed = total - passed;
    let score = ((passed as f32 / total as f32) * 100.0) as u8;

    let posture_level = match score {
        90..=100 => "GREEN",
        70..=89 => "YELLOW",
        _ => "RED",
    }
    .to_string();

    Ok(StealthPosture {
        overall_score: score,
        total_checks: total,
        passed_checks: passed,
        failed_checks: failed,
        checks,
        posture_level,
    })
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Layer runner
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Apply requested stealth layers in canonical order, recording each outcome.
/// Partial success is reported rather than collapsed into a single error.
///
/// vm_name is taken from the handle because the CPUID and hardware layers
/// address the guest by name, while the artifact layer needs the handle itself.
pub async fn apply_layers(
requirements: &StealthRequirements,
vm: &VmHandle,
profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> StealthResult<StealthReport> {
let started = Instant::now();
let mut report = StealthReport::default();

let vm_name = vm.vm_name();
let layers = requirements.ordered_layers();
let total = layers.len();

for layer in layers {
    let outcome: StealthResult<()> = match layer {
        StealthLayer::CpuIdMask => {
            let script = build_mask_script(vm_name);
            run_powershell_on_host(&script).await.map(|_| ())
        }
        StealthLayer::HardwareSpoof => patch_mac_addresses(vm_name, profile)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| StealthError::HardwareFailure {
                device_class: "network".to_string(),
                reason: e.to_string(),
            }),
        StealthLayer::ArtifactCleanup => {
            run_full_cleanup(vm)
                .await
                .map(|_: CleanupReport| ())
                .map_err(|e| StealthError::ArtifactFailure {
                    key: "registry".to_string(),
                    reason: e.to_string(),
                })
        }
        StealthLayer::TimingNormalize => patch_disk_serials(vm_name, profile)
            .await
            .map_err(|e| StealthError::TimingFailure(e.to_string())),
    };

    match outcome {
        Ok(()) => report.applied_layers.push(layer),
        Err(e) => report.failed_layers.push((layer, e.to_string())),
    }
}

report.duration_ms = started.elapsed().as_millis();

if report.applied_layers.is_empty() && total > 0 {
    return Err(StealthError::PartialApplication {
        applied: 0,
        total,
    });
}

Ok(report)
}

/// Reverse every applied layer, best-effort. Errors are collected, not fatal.
pub async fn revert_layers(
report: &StealthReport,
vm: &VmHandle,
profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> Vec<(StealthLayer, String)> {
let mut errors = Vec::new();
let vm_name = vm.vm_name();

for layer in report.applied_layers.iter().rev() {
    let result: Result<(), String> = match layer {
        StealthLayer::CpuIdMask => {
            let script = build_unmask_script(vm_name);
            run_powershell_on_host_sync(&script)
                .map(|_| ())
                .map_err(|e| e.to_string())
        }
        StealthLayer::HardwareSpoof => {
            async {
                restore_mac_addresses(vm_name)
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                restore_disk_serials(vm_name)
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                restore_smbios_profile(vm_name)
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
                Ok::<(), String>(())
            }
            .await
        }
        StealthLayer::ArtifactCleanup => run_full_restore(vm)
            .await
            .map(|_: CleanupReport| ())
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string()),
        StealthLayer::TimingNormalize => Ok(()),
    };

    if let Err(e) = result {
        errors.push((*layer, e));
    }
}

errors
}

    assert!(session.active_countermeasures.is_empty());

    let err = m
        .create_session_with_profile(TargetId::Generic, profile)

    let fake = Uuid::new_v4();

    }

    let m = manager();
    let id = m.create_session(TargetId::Generic).await.unwrap();

    m.activate_session(id).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.get_session(id).await.unwrap().state, SessionState::Active);

    m.with_session_mut(id, |s| s.transition(SessionState::Degraded))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        m.get_session(id).await.unwrap().state,
        SessionState::Degraded
    );

    m.with_session_mut(id, |s| s.transition(SessionState::Active))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(m.get_session(id).await.unwrap().state, SessionState::Active);
}

async fn invalid_transition_is_rejected() {
    let m = manager();
    let id = m.create_session(TargetId::Generic).await.unwrap();

    // Initializing -> Degraded is not in the table.
    let err = m
        .with_session_mut(id, |s| s.transition(SessionState::Degraded))
        .await
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap_err();

    match err {

fn build_tray(app: &tauri::App) -> tauri::Result<()> {
    let quit = MenuItem::with_id(app, "quit", "Quit", true, None::<&str>)?;
    let menu = Menu::with_items(app, &[&quit])?;

    let mut builder = TrayIconBuilder::new()
        .menu(&menu)
        .show_menu_on_left_click(false)
        .on_menu_event(|app, event| {
            if event.id() == "quit" {
                app.exit(0);
            }
        })
        .on_tray_icon_event(|tray, event| {
            if let TrayIconEvent::Click {
                button: MouseButton::Left,
                ..
            } = event
            {
                let app = tray.app_handle();
                if let Some(w) = app.get_webview_window("main") {
                    let _ = w.show();
                    let _ = w.set_focus();
                }
            }
        });

    if let Some(icon) = app.default_window_icon() {
        builder = builder.icon(icon.clone());
    }

    builder.build(app)?;
    Ok(())
}
