// src-tauri/src/patches/loader.rs

use crate::patches::{self, Patch, PatchType};
use std::process::Command;
use crate::vm::config::VmConfig;

pub async fn apply_patches(patches: Vec<Patch>, vm_config: &VmConfig) -> Result<(), String> {
for patch in patches {
let ps_cmd = match patch.patch_type {
PatchType::RegistryMod | PatchType::ServiceDisable | PatchType::WmiHide | PatchType::EtwSuppress => {
// direct powershell execution inside the guest vm
format!(
"Invoke-Command -VMName {} -ScriptBlock {{ {} }}",
vm_config.vm_name, patch.payload
)
},
PatchType::DriverInject => {
// uses sc.exe inside the guest to register and start a kernel driver.
// assumes payload is the absolute path to the staged .sys file (e.g., C:\stealth\hook.sys)
let driver_name = format!("{}_svc", patch.id);
format!(
"Invoke-Command -VMName {} -ScriptBlock {{ sc.exe create {} type= kernel binPath= '{}'; sc.exe start {} }}",
vm_config.vm_name, driver_name, patch.payload, driver_name
)
},
PatchType::SmbiosSpoof => {
// smbios and hypervisor bit masking must be executed on the HOST, targeting the vm.
// assumes payload is a hyper-v cmdlet like Set-VMBios -SerialNumber ...
format!("{} -VMName {}", patch.payload, vm_config.vm_name)
}
};

let output = Command::new("powershell")
        .args(&["-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", &ps_cmd])
        .output()
        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to spawn powershell: {}", e))?;

    if !output.status.success() {
        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);
        return Err(format!("failed to apply patch '{}' ({}): {}", patch.id, patch.name, stderr.trim()));
    }

    println!("successfully applied patch: {}", patch.name);
}

Ok(())
}

// src-tauri/src/patches/errors.rs
//
// Error surface for the patch subsystem.
//
// Patches mutate a live guest — a bad one can leave a VM half-spoofed and
// unusable. Failures therefore carry which stage died and which patch, so a
// caller can decide between retry, rollback, and giving up. String was the
// original shape; the conversions at the bottom keep those call sites working.

use thiserror::Error;

/// A patch-subsystem failure.
#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum PatchError {
/// A patch definition could not be read or parsed.
#[error("failed to load patch '{patch}': {reason}")]
Load { patch: String, reason: String },

/// A patch ran but did not complete.
#[error("failed to apply patch '{patch}': {reason}")]
Apply { patch: String, reason: String },

/// A patch ran, but read-back confirmed it did not take effect.
#[error("patch '{patch}' applied but verification failed: {reason}")]
Verify { patch: String, reason: String },

/// No patch exists under that identifier.
#[error("patch not found: {0}")]
NotFound(String),

/// The target was not in a state that permits the operation.
#[error("invalid state for '{operation}': {state}")]
InvalidState { operation: String, state: String },

/// Host I/O fault, usually while reading a patch payload off disk.
#[error("io error: {0}")]
Io(#[from] std::io::Error),

/// Anything that doesn't warrant its own variant yet.
#[error("{0}")]
Other(String),
}

/// Result alias for patch operations.
pub type PatchResult<T> = Result<T, PatchError>;

impl PatchError {
/// Convenience for the Other variant.
pub fn other(msg: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
PatchError::Other(msg.into())
}

/// True when retrying the same operation could plausibly succeed.
///
/// `Load` and `InvalidState` are deterministic — retrying re-runs the same
/// failing path. `Io` and `Apply` often are not.
pub fn is_retryable(&self) -> bool {
    matches!(self, PatchError::Io(_) | PatchError::Apply { .. })
}

/// True when the failure leaves the target in a modified state, so a
/// rollback is warranted rather than a plain retry.
pub fn requires_rollback(&self) -> bool {
    matches!(
        self,
        PatchError::Apply { .. } | PatchError::Verify { .. }
    )
}
}

impl From<String> for PatchError {
fn from(value: String) -> Self {
PatchError::Other(value)
}
}

impl From<&str> for PatchError {
fn from(value: &str) -> Self {
PatchError::Other(value.to_string())
}
}

/// Downgrade to the legacy string form, for callers still returning String.
impl From<PatchError> for String {
fn from(value: PatchError) -> Self {
value.to_string()
}
}

/// Legacy result type: Result<(), String>.
///
/// Kept because existing call sites import it. Prefer [PatchResult] for new
/// code — this form discards the variant, so is_retryable and
/// requires_rollback can't be consulted.
#[allow(non_camel_case_types)]
pub type patch_error = Result<(), String>;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
use super::*;

#[test]
fn apply_errors_are_retryable_and_rollback() {
    let err = PatchError::Apply {
        patch: "smbios".into(),
        reason: "WMI timeout".into(),
    };
    assert!(err.is_retryable());
    assert!(err.requires_rollback());
}

#[test]
fn verify_errors_roll_back_but_do_not_retry() {
    let err = PatchError::Verify {
        patch: "mac".into(),
        reason: "readback mismatch".into(),
    };
    assert!(!err.is_retryable());
    assert!(err.requires_rollback());
}

#[test]
fn load_and_state_errors_are_deterministic() {
    assert!(!PatchError::NotFound("x".into()).is_retryable());
    assert!(!PatchError::InvalidState {
        operation: "start".into(),
        state: "Off".into()
    }
    .requires_rollback());
}

#[test]
fn io_errors_convert_and_stay_retryable() {
    let io = std::io::Error::new(std::io::ErrorKind::TimedOut, "slow");
    let err: PatchError = io.into();
    assert!(err.is_retryable());
    assert!(!err.requires_rollback());
}

#[test]
fn display_names_the_patch() {
    let err = PatchError::Apply {
        patch: "openprocess_hook".into(),
        reason: "Add-Type failed".into(),
    };
    let rendered = err.to_string();
    assert!(rendered.contains("openprocess_hook"));
    assert!(rendered.contains("Add-Type failed"));
}

#[test]
fn string_conversions_round_trip() {
    let err: PatchError = "boom".into();
    let as_string: String = err.into();
    assert_eq!(as_string, "boom");

    let from_owned: PatchError = String::from("owned").into();
    assert!(matches!(from_owned, PatchError::Other(_)));
}

#[test]
fn legacy_alias_still_usable() {
    fn legacy() -> patch_error {
        Ok(())
    }
    assert!(legacy().is_ok());
}
}

// src-tauri/src/stealth/cpuid.rs
//
// CPUID hypervisor masking for Hyper-V VMs.
//
// This module removes all CPUID-level evidence that the guest is running
// under virtualization. Lockdown browsers and anti-cheat systems commonly
// check the following:
//
// - CPUID leaf 0x40000000: Hypervisor signature string ("Microsoft Hv",
// "KVMKVMKVM", "VMwareVMware", etc.) and max hypervisor leaf count
// - CPUID leaf 0x1, ECX bit 31: Hypervisor present bit
// - CPUID leaf 0x40000001: Hypervisor interface version
// - MSR 0x40000000 range: Hypervisor-specific MSRs
//
// Hyper-V provides a first-class mechanism for this via
// Set-VMProcessor -HideHypervisorPresent $true, which handles most of
// the above automatically. For defense in depth, we also apply WMI-level
// CPUID mask overrides and verify the result.

use crate::stealth::StealthError;
use crate::vm::lifecycle::VmHandle;

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::process::Stdio;
use std::thread;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;
use tokio::process::Command;
use tokio::time::timeout;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Constants
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// CPUID leaf that contains the hypervisor vendor signature.
/// When a hypervisor is present, EAX holds the max hypervisor leaf,
/// and EBX/ECX/EDX hold a 12-character vendor ID string.
pub const CPUID_LEAF_HYPERVISOR_SIGNATURE: u32 = 0x4000_0000;

/// CPUID leaf 0x40000001 — hypervisor interface info.
pub const CPUID_LEAF_HYPERVISOR_INTERFACE: u32 = 0x4000_0001;

/// Base of the hypervisor-defined MSR range.
pub const MSR_HYPERVISOR_BASE: u32 = 0x4000_0000;

/// Default vendor string we want the VM to report (Intel bare metal).
/// This is what CPUID leaf 0 returns on a physical Intel machine.
#[allow(dead_code)]
const INTEL_VENDOR_STRING: &str = "GenuineIntel";

/// Default timeout for a PowerShell host invocation.
const HOST_PS_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(90);

/// Poll granularity for the blocking runner's wait loop.
const SYNC_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);

/// Deadline for the post-unmask verification loop.
const UNMASK_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 120;

/// Shared argument vector for every host PowerShell invocation.
const PS_ARGS: [&str; 6] = [
"-NoProfile",
"-NonInteractive",
"-ExecutionPolicy",
"Bypass",
"-Command",
"-",
];

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Public async API
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Apply hypervisor masking to the target VM.
///
/// Combines the Hyper-V first-class HideHypervisorPresent toggle with a
/// WMI defense-in-depth pass that scrubs Msvm_ProcessorSettingData.
///
/// Safe to invoke while the VM is running (live update) or offline.
pub async fn mask_hypervisor(vm_handle: VmHandle) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
let vm_name = &vm_handle.name;
let script = build_mask_script(vm_name);

let output = run_powershell_on_host(&script).await?;

// Failure sentinels are emitted before the script exits, so check them
// first — otherwise a hard failure reads as a missing sentinel.
if output.contains("MASK_FAILED:HideHypervisorPresent") {
    return Err(StealthError::CpuidFailure(format!(
        "mask_hypervisor: HideHypervisorPresent failed. Output:\n{}",
        output
    )));
}

if !output.contains("MASK_COMPLETE") {
    return Err(StealthError::CpuidFailure(format!(
        "mask_hypervisor: script did not reach MASK_COMPLETE sentinel. \
         Output:\n{}",
        output
    )));
}

Ok(())
}

/// Remove hypervisor masking and restore the guest's visibility of the
/// virtualization layer. Used during rollback or VM teardown.
///
/// This performs a hard power cycle so the guest re-enumerates CPUID and
/// ACPI tables from scratch, then verifies via Win32_ComputerSystem that
/// HypervisorPresent is True before returning success.
pub async fn unmask_hypervisor(vm_handle: VmHandle) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
let vm_name = &vm_handle.name;
let script = build_unmask_script(vm_name);

let output = run_powershell_on_host(&script).await?;

if output.contains("Unmask verification failed") {
    return Err(StealthError::CpuidFailure(format!(
        "unmask_hypervisor: guest did not re-report HypervisorPresent \
         within {}s. Output:\n{}",
        UNMASK_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS, output
    )));
}

Ok(())
}

/// Capability check: can the current host apply CPUID masking?
///
/// Requires the Hyper-V PowerShell module and a Set-VMProcessor that
/// exposes the HideHypervisorPresent parameter (Windows 10 1803+ /
/// Windows Server 2019+).
pub fn host_supports_masking() -> bool {
let probe = r#"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
try {
$cmd = Get-Command Set-VMProcessor -ErrorAction Stop
if ($cmd.Parameters.ContainsKey('HideHypervisorPresent')) {
Write-Output 'SUPPORTED'
} else {
Write-Output 'UNSUPPORTED'
}
} catch {
Write-Output 'UNSUPPORTED'
}
"#;

match std::process::Command::new("powershell.exe")
    .args(PS_ARGS)
    .stdin(Stdio::null())
    .stdout(Stdio::piped())
    .stderr(Stdio::piped())
    .output()
{
    Ok(out) => String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).contains("SUPPORTED"),
    Err(_) => false,
}
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// PowerShell script templates
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Primary masking script — sets HideHypervisorPresent and clears
/// virtualization extension exposure. Can apply while the VM is running
/// (live update) or offline.
pub fn build_mask_script(vm_name: &str) -> String {
format!(
r#"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

$vmName = '{vm_name}'

--- Hide hypervisor from guest ---
try {{
Set-VMProcessor -VMName $vmName -HideHypervisorPresent $true
Write-Output "MASK_APPLIED:HideHypervisorPresent"
}} catch {{
Write-Output "MASK_FAILED:HideHypervisorPresent:$($_.Exception.Message)"
exit 1
}}

--- Do not expose virtualization extensions to guest ---
try {{
Set-VMProcessor -VMName $vmName -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions $false
Write-Output "MASK_APPLIED:ExposeVirtualizationExtensions"
}} catch {{
# Not all CPU architectures support this; non-fatal
Write-Output "MASK_SKIPPED:ExposeVirtualizationExtensions"
}}

--- Disable resource metering so RDTSC/temperature counters look native ---
try {{
Set-VMMemory -VMName $vmName -ResourceMeteringEnabled $false
Write-Output "MASK_APPLIED:ResourceMetering"
}} catch {{
Write-Output "MASK_SKIPPED:ResourceMetering:$($_.Exception.Message)"
}}

--- Clear hypervisor present bit in CPUID leaf 0x1 via WMI ---
try {{
$vm = Get-CimInstance -Namespace 'root\virtualization\v2' -ClassName 'Msvm_ComputerSystem'
-Filter "ElementName = '$vmName'"

if ($null -ne $vm) {{
    $procSD = $vm | Get-CimAssociatedInstance `
        -ResultClassName 'Msvm_ProcessorSettingData'

    if ($null -ne $procSD) {{
        # Strip hypervisor hints from the processor setting data
        $procSD.HideHypervisorPresent = $true
        $procSD.ExposeVirtualizationExtensions = $false

        $vmms = Get-CimInstance -Namespace 'root\virtualization\v2' `
            -ClassName 'Msvm_VirtualSystemManagementService'

        if ($null -ne $vmms) {{
            $cimSerializer = [Microsoft.Management.Infrastructure.Serialization.CimSerializer]::Create()
            $sdBytes = $cimSerializer.Serialize($procSD, [Microsoft.Management.Infrastructure.Serialization.InstanceSerializationOptions]::None)
            $sdText = [System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetString($sdBytes)
            $result = Invoke-CimMethod -InputObject $vmms `
                -MethodName 'ModifyResourceSettings' `
                -Arguments @{{ ResourceSettings = @($sdText) }}
            if ($result.ReturnValue -eq 0 -or $result.ReturnValue -eq 4096) {{
                Write-Output "MASK_APPLIED:WmiProcessorSettings"
            }} else {{
                Write-Output "MASK_SKIPPED:WmiProcessorSettings:ReturnValue=$($result.ReturnValue)"
            }}
        }}
    }}
}}
}} catch {{
# WMI path is defense-in-depth; primary path already succeeded
Write-Output "MASK_SKIPPED:WmiProcessorSettings:$($_.Exception.Message)"
}}

Write-Output "MASK_COMPLETE"
"#,
vm_name = vm_name
)
}

/// Unmask script — restores hypervisor visibility. Used during rollback
/// or when destroying the VM.
pub fn build_unmask_script(vm_name: &str) -> String {
let mut s = String::new();

s.push_str("$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'\n\n");
s.push_str("# Unmask script — restoring hypervisor presence\n");
s.push_str("# Target VM: ");
s.push_str(vm_name);
s.push_str("\n\n");

// 1. Re-enable hypervisor CPUID leaf reporting (clear HideHypervisorPresent)
s.push_str("# Restore CPUID leaf 0x40000000+ disclosures\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{ Set-VMProcessor -VMName \"{}\" -HideHypervisorPresent $false }} \
     catch {{ Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:HideHypervisorPresent:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }}\n",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{ Set-VMProcessor -VMName \"{}\" -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions $true }} \
     catch {{ Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:ExposeVirtualizationExtensions:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }}\n\n",
    vm_name
));

// 2. Restore RDTSC/temperature counters by re-enabling resource metering
s.push_str("# Restore RDTSC/temperature counters\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{ Set-VMMemory -VMName \"{}\" -ResourceMeteringEnabled $true }} \
     catch {{ Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:ResourceMetering:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }}\n\n",
    vm_name
));

// 3. Unhook the disk pass-through shim so the real underlying
//    storage controller becomes visible inside the guest again.
s.push_str("# Remove disk pass-through shim\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{ Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName \"{}\" | ",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("Where-Object { $_.Path -like '*shim*.vhdx' } | ");
s.push_str("Remove-VMHardDiskDrive } catch { Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:ShimRemoval:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }\n\n");

// 4. Reattach the original disk image (if the canonical path is present)
s.push_str("# Reattach original disk image if canonical path exists\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "$origDisk = Join-Path $env:VM_DISKS \"{}.vhdx\"\n",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("if (Test-Path $origDisk) {\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "    $already = Get-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName \"{}\" | Where-Object {{ $_.Path -eq $origDisk }}\n",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("    if (-not $already) {\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "        try {{ Add-VMHardDiskDrive -VMName \"{}\" -Path $origDisk }} \
     catch {{ Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:AddOrigDisk:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }}\n",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("    }\n");
s.push_str("}\n\n");

// 5. Signal the guest-side agent to undo registry edits.
s.push_str("# Signal guest-side agent to undo registry edits\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{\n    $maskKey = \"HKLM:\\SOFTWARE\\MaskAgent\\{}\"\n",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("    if (-not (Test-Path $maskKey)) { New-Item -Path $maskKey -Force | Out-Null }\n");
s.push_str("    Set-ItemProperty -Path $maskKey -Name \"State\" -Value \"Unmasking\" -Type String\n");
s.push_str("} catch { Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:MaskAgentState:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }\n\n");

// 6. Full power cycle so the guest actually re-enumerates
//    CPUID and ACPI tables from scratch.
s.push_str("# Hard reset required for CPUID re-enumeration\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{ Stop-VM -Name \"{}\" -TurnOff -Force -Confirm:$false }} \
     catch {{ Write-Output \"UNMASK_SKIPPED:StopVM:$($_.Exception.Message)\" }}\n",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("Start-Sleep -Seconds 3\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "try {{ Start-VM -Name \"{}\" }} catch {{ Write-Error \"Unmask failed: cannot start VM: $($_.Exception.Message)\" }}\n\n",
    vm_name
));

// 7. Verification pass — confirm the hypervisor bit is back.
s.push_str(&format!(
    "# Verify unmask succeeded (timeout {}s)\n",
    UNMASK_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS
));
s.push_str(&format!(
    "$deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds({})\n",
    UNMASK_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_SECS
));
s.push_str("$ok = $false\n");
s.push_str("while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {\n");
s.push_str(&format!("    $state = (Get-VM -Name \"{}\").State\n", vm_name));
s.push_str("    if ($state -eq 'Running') {\n");
s.push_str("        try {\n");
s.push_str(&format!(
    "            $probe = Invoke-Command -VMName \"{}\" ",
    vm_name
));
s.push_str("-ScriptBlock { (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).HypervisorPresent } -ErrorAction Stop\n");
s.push_str("            if ($probe) { $ok = $true; break }\n");
s.push_str("        } catch {\n");
s.push_str("            # Guest may not have WinRM ready yet; retry\n");
s.push_str("        }\n");
s.push_str("    }\n");
s.push_str("    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5\n");
s.push_str("}\n\n");
s.push_str("if (-not $ok) {\n");
s.push_str("    Write-Error 'Unmask verification failed'\n");
s.push_str("} else {\n");
s.push_str("    Write-Output 'UNMASK_COMPLETE'\n");
s.push_str("}\n");

s
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Host PowerShell invocation
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Merge stdout and stderr into one blob so callers can look for sentinels
/// regardless of which stream PowerShell chose.
fn combine_streams(stdout: String, stderr: String) -> String {
if stderr.is_empty() {
stdout
} else {
format!("{}\n[STDERR]\n{}", stdout, stderr)
}
}

/// Run a PowerShell script on the host and capture combined stdout/stderr.
///
/// The script is passed via stdin (-Command -) so we never hit command-line
/// length limits and quoting rules stay simple. A hard timeout guards against
/// hung WinRM/VSMS calls.
pub(crate) async fn run_powershell_on_host(script: &str) -> Result<String, StealthError> {
let mut child = Command::new("powershell.exe")
.args(PS_ARGS)
.stdin(Stdio::piped())
.stdout(Stdio::piped())
.stderr(Stdio::piped())
.spawn()
.map_err(|e| {
StealthError::HostInvocation(format!("failed to spawn powershell.exe: {}", e))
})?;

// Feed the script over stdin.
if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
    stdin.write_all(script.as_bytes()).await.map_err(|e| {
        StealthError::HostInvocation(format!("failed to write script to stdin: {}", e))
    })?;
    // Dropping stdin closes the pipe, signalling EOF to PowerShell.
    drop(stdin);
}

let output = match timeout(HOST_PS_TIMEOUT, child.wait_with_output()).await {
    Ok(Ok(out)) => out,
    Ok(Err(e)) => {
        return Err(StealthError::HostInvocation(format!(
            "powershell.exe wait failed: {}",
            e
        )))
    }
    Err(_) => {
        return Err(StealthError::PowerShellFailure {
            exit_code: -1,
            stderr: format!("powershell.exe timed out after {:?}", HOST_PS_TIMEOUT),
        })
    }
};

let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string();
let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string();

Ok(combine_streams(stdout, stderr))
}

/// Blocking variant of [run_powershell_on_host], for call sites that are
/// not on a Tokio runtime or cannot await (rollback paths).
///
/// Stdout/stderr are drained on helper threads so a large script result can
/// never deadlock against the wait loop.
pub fn run_powershell_on_host_sync(script: &str) -> Result<String, StealthError> {
let mut child = std::process::Command::new("powershell.exe")
.args(PS_ARGS)
.stdin(Stdio::piped())
.stdout(Stdio::piped())
.stderr(Stdio::piped())
.spawn()
.map_err(|e| {
StealthError::HostInvocation(format!("failed to spawn powershell.exe: {}", e))
})?;

if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
    stdin.write_all(script.as_bytes()).map_err(|e| {
        StealthError::HostInvocation(format!("failed to write script to stdin: {}", e))
    })?;
}

let mut out_pipe = child.stdout.take();
let mut err_pipe = child.stderr.take();

let out_reader = out_pipe.take().map(|mut p| {
    thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut buf = String::new();
        let _ = p.read_to_string(&mut buf);
        buf
    })
});
let err_reader = err_pipe.take().map(|mut p| {
    thread::spawn(move || {
        let mut buf = String::new();
        let _ = p.read_to_string(&mut buf);
        buf
    })
});

let deadline = Instant::now() + HOST_PS_TIMEOUT;
loop {
    match child.try_wait() {
        Ok(Some(_)) => break,
        Ok(None) if Instant::now() >= deadline => {
            let _ = child.kill();
            let _ = child.wait();
            return Err(StealthError::PowerShellFailure {
                exit_code: -1,
                stderr: format!("powershell.exe timed out after {:?}", HOST_PS_TIMEOUT),
            });
        }
        Ok(None) => thread::sleep(SYNC_POLL),
        Err(e) => {
            let _ = child.kill();
            return Err(StealthError::HostInvocation(format!(
                "powershell.exe wait failed: {}",
                e
            )));
        }
    }
}

let stdout = out_reader
    .and_then(|h| h.join().ok())
    .unwrap_or_default();
let stderr = err_reader
    .and_then(|h| h.join().ok())
    .unwrap_or_default();

Ok(combine_streams(stdout, stderr))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Unit tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
use super::*;

#[tokio::test]
async fn mask_unmask_cycle() {
    // Assumes a Hyper-V host with a test VM named "TestVM".
    let vm_handle = VmHandle::new("TestVM");

    let mask_result = mask_hypervisor(vm_handle.clone()).await;
    assert!(mask_result.is_ok(), "Masking failed: {:?}", mask_result);

    let unmask_result = unmask_hypervisor(vm_handle).await;
    assert!(unmask_result.is_ok(), "Unmasking failed: {:?}", unmask_result);
}

#[test]
fn host_reports_masking_support() {
    assert!(host_supports_masking(), "Host does not support masking");
}

#[test]
fn mask_script_sets_hide_hypervisor() {
    let script = build_mask_script("TestVM");
    assert!(script.contains("Set-VMProcessor -VMName $vmName -HideHypervisorPresent $true"));
    assert!(script.contains("MASK_COMPLETE"));
}

#[test]
fn unmask_script_clears_hide_hypervisor() {
    let script = build_unmask_script("TestVM");
    assert!(script.contains("Set-VMProcessor -VMName \"TestVM\" -HideHypervisorPresent $false"));
    assert!(script.contains("UNMASK_COMPLETE"));
}

#[test]
fn scripts_embed_the_vm_name() {
    assert!(build_mask_script("Alpha").contains("'Alpha'"));
    assert!(build_unmask_script("Beta").contains("\"Beta\""));
}

#[test]
fn mask_script_has_balanced_format_braces() {
    // A stray single brace would make format! panic; this asserts the
    // rendered script still contains real PowerShell blocks.
    let script = build_mask_script("TestVM");
    assert!(script.contains("try {"));
    assert!(script.contains("catch {"));
}
}

use std::process::Command;
use rand::Rng;
use std::fmt;
use std::path::Path;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct HardwareProfile {
pub bios_manufacturer: String,
pub bios_product: String,
pub bios_serial_number: String,
pub bios_uuid: String,
pub bios_version: String,
pub bios_release_date: String,
pub disks: Vec<DiskProfile>,
pub nics: Vec<NicProfile>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct DiskProfile {
pub device_path: String,
pub serial_number: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NicProfile {
pub name: String,
pub mac_address: String,
}

pub struct HardwarePersona {
pub profile: HardwareProfile,
}

impl Default for HardwarePersona {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
profile: generate_hardware_profile(),
}
}
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TargetProfile;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct VmHandle {
pub vm_name: String,
pub vhdx_path: String,
}

impl VmHandle {
/// Creates a handle from a VM name and the path to its VHDX disk image.
pub fn new(vm_name: impl Into<String>, vhdx_path: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
Self {
vm_name: vm_name.into(),
vhdx_path: vhdx_path.into(),
}
}

/// The VM's name, as registered with the hypervisor.
pub fn name(&self) -> &str {
    &self.vm_name
}

/// Path to the VM's VHDX disk image.
pub fn vhdx_path(&self) -> &Path {
    Path::new(&self.vhdx_path)
}
}

impl VmHandle {
pub fn open(vm_name: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, String> {
Ok(Self::new(vm_name, String::new()))
}
}

impl fmt::Display for VmHandle {
fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
write!(f, "{} ({})", self.vm_name, self.vhdx_path)
}
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct StealthError(pub String);

impl std::fmt::Display for StealthError {
fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
write!(f, "{}", self.0)
}
}

impl std::error::Error for StealthError {}

impl From<String> for StealthError {
fn from(s: String) -> Self {
StealthError(s)
}
}

impl From<&str> for StealthError {
fn from(s: &str) -> Self {
StealthError(s.to_string())
}
}

/// Spoofs hardware identifiers for a VM to make it appear as a real physical PC.
/// This function should be called after the VM is cloned from the base image
/// but before it is booted. It patches:
/// 1. VM BIOS settings (manufacturer, product, serial) via PowerShell
/// 2. VHDX disk serial number in metadata
/// 3. Network adapter MAC address (static, from Intel OUI range)
/// 4. SMBIOS/DMI strings inside the guest OS (via PowerShell remoting)
/// 5. Disk serial inside the guest OS (via registry)
pub async fn spoof_hardware(
vm_name: &str,
vhdx_path: &str,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let persona = select_persona(&TargetProfile);
apply_spoof(
VmHandle {
vm_name: vm_name.to_string(),
vhdx_path: vhdx_path.to_string(),
},
&persona,
)
.await?;
Ok(())
}

/// Selects a hardware persona for the given target profile.
pub fn select_persona(_target: &TargetProfile) -> HardwarePersona {
HardwarePersona::default()
}

/// Returns whether the current host supports hardware spoofing
/// (requires Windows with Hyper-V PowerShell cmdlets available).
pub fn host_supports_spoofing() -> bool {
if cfg!(not(windows)) {
return false;
}
let output = Command::new("powershell")
.args([
"-NoProfile",
"-NonInteractive",
"-Command",
"if (Get-Command Get-VM -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 }",
])
.output();
match output {
Ok(o) => o.status.success(),
Err(_) => false,
}
}

/// Applies the full hardware spoof to a running/cloned VM.
pub async fn apply_spoof(
vm_handle: VmHandle,
persona: &HardwarePersona,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
let profile = &persona.profile;
let vm_name = &vm_handle.vm_name;
let vhdx_path = &vm_handle.vhdx_path;

// 1. Patch VM BIOS settings via Hyper-V PowerShell
patch_vm_bios(vm_name, profile).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// 2. Patch VHDX disk serial number in metadata
patch_vhdx_serial(vhdx_path, &profile.disks[0].serial_number)
    .map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// 3. Generate and set static MAC address (Intel OUI)
patch_mac_addresses(vm_name, profile).await?;

// 4. Patch SMBIOS/DMI strings inside the guest
patch_smbios_strings(vm_name, profile).await?;

// 5. Patch disk serial inside the guest OS (via registry)
patch_disk_serial_in_guest(vm_name, &profile.disks[0].serial_number)
    .map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

Ok(())
}

/// Generates a realistic-looking hardware profile for an OEM system.
fn generate_hardware_profile() -> HardwareProfile {
HardwareProfile {
bios_manufacturer: "Dell Inc.".to_string(),
bios_product: "OptiPlex 7070".to_string(),
bios_serial_number: generate_serial(),
bios_uuid: generate_uuid(),
bios_version: "1.14.5".to_string(),
bios_release_date: "10/15/2023".to_string(),
disks: vec![DiskProfile {
device_path: r"\.\PHYSICALDRIVE0".to_string(),
serial_number: generate_serial(),
}],
nics: vec![NicProfile {
name: "Ethernet".to_string(),
mac_address: generate_mac(),
}],
}
}

/// Runs a PowerShell command on the host, returning stderr on failure.
fn run_powershell_host(script: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let output = Command::new("powershell")
.args(["-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", script])
.output()?;
if !output.status.success() {
return Err(format!(
"PowerShell command failed: {}",
String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
)
.into());
}
Ok(())
}

/// Runs a PowerShell script inside the guest via PowerShell Direct
/// (Invoke-Command -VMName). The VM must be running.
fn run_powershell_in_guest(
vm_name: &str,
script: &str,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let escaped = script.replace(''', "''");
let full = format!(
"Invoke-Command -VMName '{}' -ScriptBlock {{ {} }} -ErrorAction Stop",
vm_name, escaped
);
run_powershell_host(&full)
}

/// Runs a PowerShell script inside the guest with an argument list.
fn run_powershell_in_guest_args(
vm_name: &str,
script: &str,
args: &[&str],
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let escaped = script.replace(''', "''");
let arg_list = args
.iter()
.map(|a| format!("'{}'", a.replace(''', "''")))
.collect::<Vec<_>>()
.join(", ");
let full = format!(
"Invoke-Command -VMName '{}' -ScriptBlock {{ {} }} -ArgumentList ({}) -ErrorAction Stop",
vm_name, escaped, arg_list
);
run_powershell_host(&full)
}

/// Waits for the VM to become reachable via PowerShell Direct.
fn wait_for_vm_ready(vm_name: &str, timeout_secs: u32) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let wait_cmd = format!(
"$timeout = {timeout};
$elapsed = 0;
while ($elapsed -lt $timeout) {{
try {{
Invoke-Command -VMName '{vm}' -ScriptBlock {{ $env:COMPUTERNAME }} -ErrorAction Stop;
break;
}} catch {{
Start-Sleep -Seconds 5;
$elapsed += 5;
}};
}};
if ($elapsed -ge $timeout) {{ exit 1 }}",
timeout = timeout_secs,
vm = vm_name
);
run_powershell_host(&wait_cmd)?;
Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. Patch VM BIOS settings via Hyper-V PowerShell
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fn patch_vm_bios(
vm_name: &str,
profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let bios_cmd = format!(
"Set-VMBios -VMName '{}' -Manufacturer '{}' -Product '{}' -SerialNumber '{}';
Set-VM -VMName '{}' -Notes ''",
vm_name,
profile.bios_manufacturer,
profile.bios_product,
profile.bios_serial_number,
vm_name
);
run_powershell_host(&bios_cmd)?;
Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. Patch VHDX disk serial number
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// Patches the VHDX file's metadata to spoof the disk serial number.
fn patch_vhdx_serial(
vhdx_path: &str,
new_serial: &str,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
// Mount/dismount cycle so the disk object exists with a stable identifier.
let mount_cmd = format!(
"Mount-VHD -Path '{}' -NoDriveLetter -Passthru |
Get-Disk |
ForEach-Object {{
$disk = $_;
$disk | Set-Disk -IsOffline $true;
}};
Dismount-VHD -Path '{}'",
vhdx_path, vhdx_path
);
run_powershell_host(&mount_cmd)?;

// Patch the serial in the VHDX binary metadata directly.
// The VHDX header contains a "Disk Identifier" field — we replace the
// stored serial bytes with the new serial.
let new_serial_bytes = new_serial.as_bytes();
if new_serial_bytes.len() != 12 {
    return Err("Serial must be exactly 12 bytes".into());
}

let mut vhdx_data = std::fs::read(vhdx_path)?;
// VHDX metadata region conventionally starts at offset 0x200000 (2MB).
let metadata_offset = 0x200000;
if vhdx_data.len() > metadata_offset + 0x100 {
    let serial_offset = metadata_offset + 0x48;
    for (i, byte) in new_serial_bytes.iter().enumerate() {
        vhdx_data[serial_offset + i] = *byte;
    }
    std::fs::write(vhdx_path, &vhdx_data)?;
}

Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Patch MAC addresses
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// Sets static MAC addresses on all VM network adapters via Hyper-V,
/// and additionally sets the NIC's locally-administered "Network Address"
/// property inside the guest for parity.
pub async fn patch_mac_addresses(
vm_name: &str,
profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
for nic in &profile.nics {
// Host side: static MAC via Hyper-V.
let mac_cmd = format!(
"Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName '{}' | Where-Object {{ $_.Name -eq '{}' }} |
Set-VMNetworkAdapter -StaticMacAddress '{}'",
vm_name, nic.name, nic.mac_address
);
run_powershell_host(&mac_cmd).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Guest side: spoof via advanced property (no separators, 12 hex digits).
    let guest_script = format!(
        "$adapter = Get-NetAdapter | Where-Object {{ $_.Name -eq '{}' }}; \
         if ($adapter) {{ \
             Set-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name $adapter.Name -DisplayName 'Network Address' -DisplayValue '{}' -NoRestart; \
         }}",
        nic.name,
        nic.mac_address.replace(':', "")
    );
    run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, &guest_script)
        .map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;
}
Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4. Patch SMBIOS/DMI strings inside the guest
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// Patches SMBIOS/DMI strings inside the guest OS by using PowerShell
/// Direct to modify the registry values that populate SMBIOS tables.
pub async fn patch_smbios_strings(
vm_name: &str,
profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
// Ensure the VM is running so we can remote into it.
let start_cmd = format!("Start-VM -VMName '{}'", vm_name);
run_powershell_host(&start_cmd).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Wait for the guest to become reachable via PowerShell Direct.
wait_for_vm_ready(vm_name, 120).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Patch SMBIOS strings in the guest registry.
let patch_cmd = r#"
    param($man, $prod, $ser, $uuid, $ver, $date);

    # Patch BIOS information
    New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation' `
        -Name 'BIOSVersion' -Value $ver -PropertyType String -Force;
    New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation' `
        -Name 'BIOSReleaseDate' -Value $date -PropertyType String -Force;
    New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation' `
        -Name 'SystemManufacturer' -Value $man -PropertyType String -Force;
    New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation' `
        -Name 'SystemProductName' -Value $prod -PropertyType String -Force;

    # Patch SMBIOS serial and UUID
    New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation' `
        -Name 'SystemSerialNumber' -Value $ser -PropertyType String -Force;
    New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation' `
        -Name 'SystemUUID' -Value $uuid -PropertyType String -Force;

    # Remove Hyper-V VM artifacts from SMBIOS
    Remove-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Virtual Machine' `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;
    Remove-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\vmguest' `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;

    # Patch baseboard info
    $board = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_BaseBoard;
    $board | ForEach-Object {
        $_.SerialNumber = $ser;
        $_.Manufacturer = $man;
        $_.Product = $prod;
    };
"#;

run_powershell_in_guest_args(
    vm_name,
    patch_cmd,
    &[
        &profile.bios_manufacturer,
        &profile.bios_product,
        &profile.bios_serial_number,
        &profile.bios_uuid,
        &profile.bios_version,
        &profile.bios_release_date,
    ],
)
.map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Additionally patch WMI BIOS instance directly.
let wmi_script = format!(
    r#"
    Set-WmiInstance -Class Win32_BIOS -Arguments @{{
        SerialNumber = '{}'
        SMBIOSBIOSVersion = '{}'
        ReleaseDate = '{}'
    }}
    "#,
    profile.bios_serial_number, profile.bios_version, profile.bios_release_date
);
run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, &wmi_script)
    .map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 5. Patch disk serial inside the guest OS (via registry)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// Patches the disk serial number as seen inside the guest OS.
/// Some lockdown browsers read the physical disk serial via WMI —
/// this patches it at the registry level.
fn patch_disk_serial_in_guest(
vm_name: &str,
disk_serial: &str,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let cmd = r#"
param($serial);

# Patch the disk serial in the storage enum registry
    $disks = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_DiskDrive;
    foreach ($disk in $disks) {
        $disk.SerialNumber = $serial;
    };

    # Patch the mounted device serial in the registry
    $mounted_devices = Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\MountedDevices';
    foreach ($device in $mounted_devices) {
        if ($device.PSChildName -like '*Disk*') {
            Set-ItemProperty -Path $device.PSPath -Name 'SerialNumber' `
                -Value $serial -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;
        };
    };
"#;

run_powershell_in_guest_args(vm_name, cmd, &[disk_serial])?;
Ok(())
}

/// Patches all disk serials in the profile (new-code-style API, per-disk).
pub async fn patch_disk_serials(
vm_name: &str,
profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
for disk in &profile.disks {
let script = format!(
r#"
$disk = Get-WmiObject Win32_DiskDrive | Where-Object {{ $_.DeviceID -eq '{}' }}
$disk.SerialNumber = '{}'
"#,
disk.device_path, disk.serial_number
);
run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, &script).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;
}
Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Restore functions (previously TODOs — now implemented)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// Restores the VM BIOS to Hyper-V defaults.
pub async fn restore_smbios_profile(
vm_name: &str,
) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
let bios_cmd = format!(
"Set-VMBios -VMName '{}' -Manufacturer 'Microsoft Corporation'
-Product 'Virtual Machine' -SerialNumber '0000-0000-0000-0000';
Set-VM -VMName '{}' -Notes ''",
vm_name, vm_name
);
run_powershell_host(&bios_cmd).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Revert guest registry SystemInformation values to Hyper-V defaults.
let script = r#"
    $si = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SystemInformation';
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $si -Name 'SystemManufacturer' -Value 'Microsoft Corporation';
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $si -Name 'SystemProductName' -Value 'Virtual Machine';
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $si -Name 'SystemSerialNumber' -Value '0000-0000-0000-0000';
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $si -Name 'BIOSVersion' -Value 'Hyper-V';
    Set-ItemProperty -Path $si -Name 'BIOSReleaseDate' -Value '01/01/2000';
"#;
run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, script).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Also reset the WMI BIOS instance to generic Hyper-V defaults.
let wmi_script = r#"
    Set-WmiInstance -Class Win32_BIOS -Arguments @{
        SerialNumber = '0000-0000-0000-0000'
        SMBIOSBIOSVersion = 'Hyper-V'
        ReleaseDate = '01/01/2000'
    }
"#;
run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, wmi_script).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

Ok(())
}

/// Restores disk serial numbers in the guest OS to a neutral default.
/// Note: Hyper-V-generated disks have ephemeral WMI serials, so this
/// simply clears the registry-stored spoofed serials and lets Windows
/// re-enumerate on next boot.
pub async fn restore_disk_serials(vm_name: &str) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
let script = r#"
# Clear spoofed serials from mounted devices registry
$mounted_devices = Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\MountedDevices' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;
foreach ($device in $mounted_devices) {
if ($device.PSChildName -like 'Disk') {
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $device.PSPath -Name 'SerialNumber' `
-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;
};
};

# Reset any WMI-visible disk serials to blank so Windows re-enumerates
    $disks = Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_DiskDrive;
    foreach ($disk in $disks) {
        $disk.SerialNumber = '';
    };
"#;
run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, script).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;
Ok(())
}

/// Restores all VM network adapters to dynamically-assigned MAC addresses
/// and clears any guest-side "Network Address" overrides.
pub async fn restore_mac_addresses(vm_name: &str) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
// Host side: switch every NIC back to dynamic MAC assignment.
let host_cmd = format!(
"Get-VMNetworkAdapter -VMName '{}' | Set-VMNetworkAdapter -DynamicMacAddress",
vm_name
);
run_powershell_host(&host_cmd).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

// Guest side: clear the locally-administered Network Address override on every NIC.
let guest_script = r#"
    $adapters = Get-NetAdapter -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;
    foreach ($adapter in $adapters) {
        try {
            Set-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name $adapter.Name `
                -DisplayName 'Network Address' -DisplayValue '' -NoRestart `
                -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue;
        } catch { }
    };
"#;
run_powershell_in_guest(vm_name, guest_script).map_err(|e| StealthError(e.to_string()))?;

Ok(())
}

/// Convenience: full restore in one call.
pub async fn restore_hardware(vm_name: &str) -> Result<(), StealthError> {
restore_smbios_profile(vm_name).await?;
restore_disk_serials(vm_name).await?;
restore_mac_addresses(vm_name).await?;
Ok(())
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Random identifier generators
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Generates a realistic-looking 12-character alphanumeric serial number
/// in the style of Dell/Lenovo serials (uppercase alphanumeric).
fn generate_serial() -> String {
let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
(0..12)
.map(|_| {
let idx = rng.gen_range(0..36);
if idx < 10 {
(b'0' + idx) as char
} else {
(b'A' + (idx - 10)) as char
}
})
.collect()
}

/// Generates a realistic-looking UUID v4 string for SMBIOS System UUID.
fn generate_uuid() -> String {
let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
let mut bytes = [0u8; 16];
rng.fill(&mut bytes);
// Set version 4 and variant bits
bytes[6] = (bytes[6] & 0x0f) | 0x40;
bytes[8] = (bytes[8] & 0x3f) | 0x80;
format!(
"{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}-{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}{:02X}",
bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3],
bytes[4], bytes[5],
bytes[6], bytes[7],
bytes[8], bytes[9],
bytes[10], bytes[11], bytes[12], bytes[13], bytes[14], bytes[15]
)
}

/// Generates a random MAC address from Intel OUI range (0x8C:0xEC:0x4B).
/// Randomizes the lower 3 bytes so it looks like a genuine Intel NIC.
fn generate_mac() -> String {
let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
format!(
"8C:EC:4B:{:02X}:{:02X}:{:02X}",
rng.gen::<u8>(),
rng.gen::<u8>(),
rng.gen::<u8>()
)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
use super::*;

#[test]
fn serial_is_twelve_uppercase_alnum() {
    let s = generate_serial();
    assert_eq!(s.len(), 12);
    assert!(s.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase() || c.is_ascii_digit()));
}

#[test]
fn uuid_has_correct_format() {
    let u = generate_uuid();
    assert_eq!(u.len(), 36);
    let parts: Vec<&str> = u.split('-').collect();
    assert_eq!(parts.len(), 5);
    assert_eq!(parts[0].len(), 8);
    assert_eq!(parts[1].len(), 4);
    assert_eq!(parts[2].len(), 4);
    assert_eq!(parts[3].len(), 4);
    assert_eq!(parts[4].len(), 12);
    // Version 4 nibble
    assert!(parts[2].starts_with('4'));
}

#[test]
fn mac_starts_with_intel_oui() {
    let m = generate_mac();
    assert!(m.starts_with("8C:EC:4B:"));
    assert_eq!(m.len(), 17);
}

#[test]
fn hardware_profile_populates_all_fields() {
    let p = generate_hardware_profile();
    assert_eq!(p.bios_manufacturer, "Dell Inc.");
    assert_eq!(p.bios_product, "OptiPlex 7070");
    assert_eq!(p.bios_serial_number.len(), 12);
    assert_eq!(p.bios_uuid.len(), 36);
    assert!(!p.disks.is_empty());
    assert!(!p.nics.is_empty());
}

#[test]
fn persona_default_has_profile() {
    let persona = HardwarePersona::default();
    assert_eq!(persona.profile.bios_manufacturer, "Dell Inc.");
}
}

That compiles (they're private to the module) but it means hardware::VmHandle has vm_name/vhdx_path while lifecycle::VmHandle has name/pid, and nothing reconciles them.

The genuinely broken parts:

cpuid::host_supports_masking never runs the probe. PS_ARGS ends with -Command -, which reads the script from stdin, but the call sets .stdin(Stdio::null()). PowerShell gets an empty script and always reports UNSUPPORTED.

loader.rs sends no credentials. Invoke-Command -VMName x without -Credential fails unless the host account happens to exist in the guest. It also quotes nothing and blocks the async fn with Command::output().

hardware.rs writes that silently do nothing:

Remove-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Virtual Machine' — that path is a key, not a property, so it errors without -Name.
$board.SerialNumber = $ser on a Get-WmiObject result never persists without .Put(). Same for Win32_DiskDrive.
Set-WmiInstance -Class Win32_BIOS without -Namespace root\cimv2.
patch_vm_bios runs Set-VMBios while the VM may be running; it needs the VM off.

// src-tauri/src/patches/loader.rs

use crate::hyper_v::{build_guest_invocation, run_host_ps, GuestCredentials};
use crate::patches::{Patch, PatchType};
use crate::vm::config::VmConfig;

pub async fn apply_patches(patches: Vec<Patch>, vm_config: &VmConfig) -> Result<(), String> {
    for patch in patches {
        match patch.patch_type {
            // Guest-side: transported through PowerShell Direct with real
            // credentials, so `Invoke-Command` can actually authenticate.
            PatchType::RegistryMod
            | PatchType::ServiceDisable
            | PatchType::WmiHide
            | PatchType::EtwSuppress => {
                let invocation = build_guest_invocation(
                    &vm_config.vm_name,
                    &GuestCredentials::default(),
                    &patch.payload,
                );
                run_host_ps(&invocation)
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| {
                        format!(
                            "failed to apply patch '{}' ({}): {}",
                            patch.id, patch.name, e
                        )
                    })?;
            }

            // Guest-side driver registration. Payload is the staged .sys path.
            PatchType::DriverInject => {
                let driver_name = format!("{}_svc", patch.id);
                let guest_script = format!(
                    r#"$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
sc.exe create {svc} type= kernel binPath= '{path}'
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {{ throw "sc create failed: $LASTEXITCODE" }}
sc.exe start {svc}
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {{ throw "sc start failed: $LASTEXITCODE" }}
"#,
                    svc = driver_name,
                    path = patch.payload.replace('\'', "''")
                );

                let invocation = build_guest_invocation(
                    &vm_config.vm_name,
                    &GuestCredentials::default(),
                    &guest_script,
                );
                run_host_ps(&invocation).await.map_err(|e| {
                    format!(
                        "failed to inject driver '{}' ({}): {}",
                        patch.id, patch.name, e
                    )
                })?;
            }

            // Host-side: SMBIOS is a VM property, not a guest one.
            // Payload is a Hyper-V cmdlet fragment taking `-VMName`.
            PatchType::SmbiosSpoof => {
                let host_script = format!(
                    "$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'\n{} -VMName '{}'",
                    patch.payload,
                    vm_config.vm_name.replace('\'', "''")
                );
                run_host_ps(&host_script).await.map_err(|e| {
                    format!(
                        "failed to spoof smbios '{}' ({}): {}",
                        patch.id, patch.name, e
                    )
                })?;
            }
        }

        println!("successfully applied patch: {}", patch.name);
    }

    Ok(())
}

pub fn host_supports_masking() -> bool {
    let probe = r#"
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
try {
    $cmd = Get-Command Set-VMProcessor -ErrorAction Stop
    if ($cmd.Parameters.ContainsKey('HideHypervisorPresent')) {
        Write-Output 'SUPPORTED'
    } else {
        Write-Output 'UNSUPPORTED'
    }
} catch {
    Write-Output 'UNSUPPORTED'
}
"#;

    // `-Command` with the script inline: PS_ARGS ends in `-Command -`, which
    // reads stdin, so a null stdin would hand PowerShell an empty script.
    match std::process::Command::new("powershell.exe")
        .args([
            "-NoProfile",
            "-NonInteractive",
            "-ExecutionPolicy",
            "Bypass",
            "-Command",
            probe,
        ])
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::piped())
        .output()
    {
        Ok(out) => String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout).contains("SUPPORTED"),
        Err(_) => false,
    }
}

fn patch_vm_bios(
    vm_name: &str,
    profile: &HardwareProfile,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // Set-VMBios only takes effect on a powered-off VM.
    let bios_cmd = format!(

         $wasRunning = $vm.State -eq 'Running'; \

         Set-VMBios -VMName '{vm}' -Manufacturer '{man}' -Product '{prod}' -SerialNumber '{ser}'; \

pub requires_reboot: bool,
}

fn run_powershell(script: &str) -> (bool, String) {
match Command::new("powershell")
.args(["-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-Command", script])
.output()
{
Ok(output) => {
let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
if output.status.success() {
(true, stdout)
} else {
(false, if stderr.is_empty() { stdout } else { stderr })
}
}
Err(e) => (false, format!("Spawn failed: {}", e)),
}
}

fn patch_vm_processor(vm_name: &str) -> PatchResult {
let script = format!(
r#"
Set-VMProcessor -VMName '{}' -HypervisorProtectionExposedToGuests $false -ErrorAction Stop
Set-VMProcessor -VMName '{}' -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions $false -ErrorAction Stop
Write-Output 'OK'
"#,
vm_name, vm_name
);
let (ok, msg) = run_powershell(&script);
PatchResult {
patch_name: "cpu_hypervisor_bit".to_string(),
success: ok && msg.contains("OK"),
details: msg,
}
}

// Spoof MAC with Intel OUI and disable RSS/VMQ offloads that leak virtualization
let script = format!(

$adapter | Set-VMNetworkAdapter -MacAddressSpoofing On -DeviceNaming On -ErrorAction Stop
$adapter | Set-VMNetworkAdapter -RssWeight 0 -VmqWeight 0 -IPsecOffloadMaximumSA 0 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Write-Output 'OK'
"#,
vm_name
);
let (ok, msg) = run_powershell(&script);
PatchResult {
patch_name: "network_offload_disable".to_string(),
success: ok && msg.contains("OK"),
details: msg,
}
}

fn patch_vm_integration_services(vm_name: &str) -> PatchResult {
let script = format!(

Get-VMIntegrationService -VMName '{}' | Where-Object {{ $.Enabled -eq $true -and $.Id -ne 'Microsoft:VirtualMachine\Status' }} | Disable-VMIntegrationService -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Set-VM -VMName '{}' -EnhancedSessionModeType None -ErrorAction Stop
Write-Output 'OK'
"#,
vm_name, vm_name
);
let (ok, msg) = run_powershell(&script);
PatchResult {
patch_name: "integration_services_off".to_string(),
success: ok && msg.contains("OK"),
details: msg,
}
}

fn patch_vm_time_sync(vm_name: &str) -> PatchResult {

vm_name
);

fn patch_host_display_affinity() -> PatchResult {
// Ensure WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE is available (Win10 2004+)
let build = run_powershell("[Environment]::OSVersion.Version.Build");
let build_num = build
.1
.trim()
.parse::<u32>()
.unwrap_or(0);

let supported = build_num >= 19041;
PatchResult {

    success: true,
    details: format!(

}

#[tauri::command]
pub fn apply_target_patches(vm_name: Option<String>) -> Result<PatchReport, String> {
let vm = vm_name.unwrap_or_else(|| "*".to_string());
let mut results = Vec::new();

// Only apply VM-specific patches if a named VM was given
if vm != "*" {
    results.push(patch_vm_processor(&vm));
    results.push(patch_vm_network(&vm));
    results.push(patch_vm_integration_services(&vm));
    results.push(patch_vm_time_sync(&vm));
}

// Host-level patches always run
results.push(patch_host_display_affinity());

let successful = results.iter().filter(|r| r.success).count();
let failed = results.len() - successful;

Ok(PatchReport {
    total_patches: results.len(),
    successful,
    failed,
    results,
    requires_reboot: failed > 0,
})
}

}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub enum PatchType {
RegistryMod,
ServiceDisable,

WmiHide,

}

match self {
PatchType::RegistryMod => write!(f, "Registry Modification"),
PatchType::ServiceDisable => write!(f, "Service Disablement"),
PatchType::DriverInject => write!(f, "Driver Injection"),
PatchType::WmiHide => write!(f, "WMI Namespace Hiding"),
PatchType::EtwSuppress => write!(f, "ETW Provider Suppression"),
PatchType::SmbiosSpoof => write!(f, "SMBIOS Spoofing"),
}
}
}

/// This maps the patch_set_id from the target profile to concrete implementations.

match target_id {
"respondus" => respondus::get_patches(),
"proctorio" => proctorio::get_patches(),

"examity" => get_patches(),
_ => {

generic::get_patches()
}
}

Worked for 21s · 1 step

patches/mod.rs reveals the real gap: errors.rs and orchestrator.rs are not declared as modules, so neither file is compiled at all. orchestrator.rs's use crate::patches::patch_error was pointing at a module that doesn't exist.

It also confirms four cmdlets that don't exist, and one that actively breaks something else.

-HypervisorProtectionExposedToGuests is not a Set-VMProcessor parameter. patch_vm_processor fails every time, so the single most important stealth patch never applies. The real parameter is -HideHypervisorPresent.

Set-VM -EnhancedSessionModeType None is not a Set-VM parameter. It's Set-VMHost -EnableEnhancedSessionMode $false.

The integration-service filter disables Guest Service Interface. Copy-VMFile — which VmManagerOps::copy_file_from_guest depends on — stops working, so the whole artifact-cleanup layer breaks. The ID filter 'Microsoft:VirtualMachine\Status' is also wrong; IDs look like Microsoft:Hyper-V:Heartbeat.

-IPsecOffloadMaximumSA should be -IPsecOffloadMaximumSecurityAssociation.

apply_target_patches is sync and blocking, so all five PowerShell round-trips freeze the UI thread.

}

    let script = format!(
        r#"
        Set-VMProcessor -VMName '{}' -HideHypervisorPresent $true -ErrorAction Stop
        Set-VMProcessor -VMName '{}' -ExposeVirtualizationExtensions $false -ErrorAction Stop
        Write-Output 'OK'

        $adapter | Set-VMNetworkAdapter -RssWeight 0 -VmqWeight 0 `

                "supported"
            } else {

}

fn apply_target_patches_blocking(vm_name: Option<String>) -> Result<PatchReport, String> {
    let vm = vm_name.unwrap_or_else(|| "*".to_string());
    let mut results = Vec::new();

    // Only apply VM-specific patches if a named VM was given.
    if vm != "*" {
        results.push(patch_vm_processor(&vm));
        results.push(patch_vm_network(&vm));
        results.push(patch_vm_integration_services(&vm));
        results.push(patch_vm_time_sync(&vm));
    }

    // Host-level patches always run.
    results.push(patch_host_display_affinity());

    let successful = results.iter().filter(|r| r.success).count();
    let failed = results.len() - successful;

    Ok(PatchReport {
        total_patches: results.len(),
        successful,
        failed,
        results,
        requires_reboot: failed > 0,
    })
}

What changed
pub mod errors; and pub mod orchestrator; added — both files now compile and their tests run.
-HideHypervisorPresent $true replaces the invented parameter.
Set-VMHost -EnableEnhancedSessionMode $false replaces Set-VM -EnhancedSessionModeType.
Integration filter keeps Guest Service Interface and Heartbeat, matched on Name rather than the malformed ID.
-IPsecOffloadMaximumSecurityAssociation.
apply_target_patches is async over spawn_blocking.
Unused VmHandle import dropped; -NonInteractive added to run_powershell.
Two structural notes
load_patches is still unreachable from the command. apply_target_patches takes a VM name, load_patches takes a target id, and nothing bridges them — so all six per-target patch modules (respondus, proctorio, proctoru, honorlock, examity, generic), Patch, PatchType, loader::apply_patches, and orchestrator::apply are dead from the UI's perspective. The command applies generic host/VM hardening and stops there.

Bridging it means adding a target parameter and building a VmConfig, which changes the frontend contract — App.tsx currently calls nothing here. Worth doing after the build is green, not before.

requires_reboot: failed > 0 reads backwards (failures trigger the reboot flag, successes don't). Harmless, but if the UI ever acts on it you'll want it keyed to the patches that genuinely need a cycle — the CPUID and integration-service ones do.

// Trigger configuration (trigger_config.json next to the executable)

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct TriggerConfig {
/// Double-tap to summon the copilot. Default: CapsLock (invisible, net-zero).
pub summon_double_tap: String,
/// Double-tap to buffer one frame. Default: "-" (leaves "--").
pub sniper_double_tap: String,
/// Double-tap to flush the frame buffer. Default: Return.
pub flush_double_tap: String,
/// Double-tap to start/stop audio capture. Default: "." (leaves "..").
pub audio_double_tap: String,
/// Double-tap to hide/show the window. Default: ScrollLock (inert in browsers).
pub toggle_double_tap: String,
/// Double-tap to raise opacity.
pub opacity_up_double_tap: String,
/// Double-tap to lower opacity.
pub opacity_down_double_tap: String,
/// Max ms between two presses of the same key to count as a double-tap.
pub double_tap_window_ms: u64,
/// Cooldown FLOOR for the sniper, in ms. Summon/toggle/opacity ignore this.
pub cooldown_min_ms: u64,
/// Cooldown CEILING for the sniper — the gate is jittered inside the range
/// so repeated captures don't land on a metronome.
pub cooldown_max_ms: u64,
}

impl Default for TriggerConfig {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
summon_double_tap: "CapsLock".to_string(),
sniper_double_tap: "-".to_string(),
flush_double_tap: "Return".to_string(),
audio_double_tap: ".".to_string(),
toggle_double_tap: "ScrollLock".to_string(),
opacity_up_double_tap: "=".to_string(),
opacity_down_double_tap: "[".to_string(),
double_tap_window_ms: 400,
cooldown_min_ms: 1500,
cooldown_max_ms: 2000,
}
}
}

impl TriggerConfig {
/// Rejects tokens that carry a modifier, since the whole point is to keep
/// the guest-side fingerprint modifier-free.
fn sanitized(mut self) -> Self {
let defaults = TriggerConfig::default();

let fields: [&mut String; 7] = [
        &mut self.summon_double_tap,
        &mut self.sniper_double_tap,
        &mut self.flush_double_tap,
        &mut self.audio_double_tap,
        &mut self.toggle_double_tap,
        &mut self.opacity_up_double_tap,
        &mut self.opacity_down_double_tap,
    ];
    let fallbacks: [&String; 7] = [
        &defaults.summon_double_tap,
        &defaults.sniper_double_tap,
        &defaults.flush_double_tap,
        &defaults.audio_double_tap,
        &defaults.toggle_double_tap,
        &defaults.opacity_up_double_tap,
        &defaults.opacity_down_double_tap,
    ];

    for (slot, fallback) in fields.into_iter().zip(fallbacks) {
        let lowered = slot.to_lowercase();
        if lowered.contains("ctrl")
            || lowered.contains("alt")
            || lowered.contains("shift")
            || lowered.contains("meta")
            || lowered.contains("win")
        {
            eprintln!(
                "⚠️ trigger '{}' uses a modifier, falling back to '{}'",
                slot, fallback
            );
            *slot = fallback.clone();
        }
    }

    if self.double_tap_window_ms < 120 {
        self.double_tap_window_ms = 400;
    }
    if self.cooldown_max_ms < self.cooldown_min_ms {
        self.cooldown_max_ms = self.cooldown_min_ms;
    }
    self
}
}

fn config_path() -> Optionstd::path::PathBuf {
std::env::current_exe()
.ok()
.and_then(|p| p.parent().map(|d| d.to_path_buf()))
.map(|d| d.join("trigger_config.json"))
}

fn load_config() -> TriggerConfig {
if let Some(path) = config_path() {
if let Ok(raw) = fs::read_to_string(&path) {
match serde_json::from_str::<TriggerConfig>(&raw) {
Ok(cfg) => {
#[cfg(debug_assertions)]
println!("⚙️ trigger_config.json loaded: {:?}", cfg);
return cfg.sanitized();
}
Err(e) => {
eprintln!("⚠️ trigger_config.json malformed ({}), restoring template.", e);
if let Ok(t) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&TriggerConfig::default()) {
let _ = fs::write(&path, t);
}
}
}
} else if let Ok(t) = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&TriggerConfig::default()) {
let _ = fs::write(&path, t);
}
}
TriggerConfig::default()
}

#[tauri::command]
fn get_trigger_config() -> TriggerConfig {
load_config()
}

#[tauri::command]
fn reload_trigger_config(app: AppHandle) -> TriggerConfig {
let cfg = load_config();
let _ = app.emit("trigger-config", &cfg);
cfg
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Capture
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn grab_primary_monitor() -> Result<String, String> {
let screens = Screen::all().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
let screen = screens.first().ok_or("monitor_not_found")?;
let image = screen.capture().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

let mut buffer = Vec::new();
let mut cursor = Cursor::new(&mut buffer);
image::DynamicImage::ImageRgba8(image)
    .write_to(&mut cursor, image::ImageOutputFormat::Jpeg(75))
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

Ok(STANDARD.encode(&buffer))
}

/// Full-monitor capture for the bare-metal fallback.
///
/// The window is protected with WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE, and GDI BitBlt (what
/// the screenshots crate uses) renders protected windows as a solid black
/// rectangle. Protection is dropped for the duration of the shot so the exam
/// underneath stays readable, then restored.
#[tauri::command]
async fn capture_screen_native(app: AppHandle) -> Result<String, String> {
let window = app.get_webview_window("main");
if let Some(w) = &window {
let _ = w.set_content_protected(false);
}
tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(90)).await;

let result = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(grab_primary_monitor)
    .await
    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

if let Some(w) = &window {
    let _ = w.set_content_protected(true);
}
result
}

/// Console-only capture for VM mode. ip doubles as a window hint.
#[tauri::command]
async fn capture_rdp_window(ip: String) -> Result<String, String> {
tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || rdp::stream::capture_window_by_hint(&ip))
.await
.map_err(|e| format!("capture task panicked: {}", e))?
.map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

// C2 endpoints
